articles.title: Ohio mayor responds to Travis Kelce’s $5.35 million property decision after neighbors raise concerns
articles.summary: NFL News: Travis Kelce’s return to his Ohio roots has come with an unexpected neighborhood debate. The NFL star recently bought a sprawling lakefront property i.
articles.body: Travis Kelce’s return to his Ohio roots has come with an unexpected neighborhood debate. The NFL star recently bought a sprawling lakefront property in Bratenahl, near Cleveland, hoping to have a private retreat close to where he grew up. But plans for a new fence have already raised concerns among nearby residents about their views of Lake Erie.Travis Kelce’s Bratenahl home sparks fence concernsThe property is far more than a typical luxury home. The 21,000-square-foot Tudor-style estate sits on roughly 3.5 acres and includes eight bedrooms, 11 bathrooms, a theater, wine cellar, fitness center and sauna. A separate two-bedroom guest cottage is also part of the estate.One of its more unusual features is a former Prohibition-era speakeasy. The space has since been converted into a game room, adding another piece of history to the already distinctive property.The reported fence plans became a talking point among neighbors after concerns emerged that the structure could interfere with views of the lake. According to reports, the original proposal included extending the fence all the way toward the beach. That portion was later dropped following discussions between the property owners and nearby residents.Bratenahl Mayor Keith Benjamin said the village has experience welcoming high-profile residents while respecting their need for privacy.“We’re used to this in Bratenahl,” Benjamin told The New York Times. “Being a welcoming community includes giving people the space to be at home, whether they’re an average resident or the most famous person in the world.”Benjamin also stressed that privacy should not come at the expense of being a good neighbor.“We take pride in being a welcoming community where people can feel connected to their lives and also feel comfortable enjoying their private lives,” Keith Benjamin told News 5. “You know, part of being a good neighbor is offering a warm welcome and also giving people the privacy and the space to simply be at home — no matter who lives next door.”Travis Kelce’s Ohio roots make the property personalFor Kelce, the Bratenahl purchase carries a significance that goes beyond luxury. He grew up in nearby Cleveland Heights with his older brother Jason Kelce, who later became a longtime Philadelphia Eagles center.That connection helps explain why an Ohio property could appeal to the Chiefs star. Rather than simply adding another expensive residence, the home gives him a chance to stay close to an area tied to his childhood.Still, the attention surrounding the estate shows why privacy is likely to remain a major concern. The couple has already attracted interest from people curious about the property. A September 3 report from The New York Times noted that a local dog walker saw teenage girls photographing the home from a passing car.Kelce has experienced the risks of unwanted attention firsthand. His previous Leawood, Kansas, home was burglarized on October 7, 2024, while he was away attending a Chiefs game. That experience makes the desire for stronger security understandable.Bratenahl itself is no stranger to notable residents. The village has counted businessman James Salisbury, actor Jim Backus and former Cardinals owner Helene Hathaway Robison Britton among its historic residents. One local property was also featured on “Keeping Up With the Kardashians.”For now, the fence dispute appears to be moving toward a compromise rather than a major neighborhood clash. Kelce may have found his Ohio retreat, but making it feel like home will involve balancing privacy, security and the lake views that make the community special.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Kyler Murray's OT Wishes He 'Took a Shot At' Packers' Bullard for Hit That Injured Vikings QB
articles.summary: Veteran quarterback Kyler Murray's debut with the Minnesota Vikings was cut short when he suffered a concussion just 11 plays into Sunday's season opener against the Green Bay Packers.
articles.body:
Veteran quarterback Kyler Murray's debut with the Minnesota Vikings was cut short when he suffered a concussion just 11 plays into Sunday's season opener against the Green Bay Packers.

Murray scrambled on a third-down play in the first quarter before taking a big hit from Packers defensive end Lukas Van Ness and safety Javon Bullard, the latter of whom was flagged for unnecessary roughness. Vikings right tackle Brian O'Neill shoved Bullard in defense of his quarterback, and he said after the game that he wished he had done more.

"It was so bang, bang," O'Neill said, per ESPN's Kevin Seifert . "You don't want to freak out if you're wrong. I was probably wrong to not freak out more than that. So I kind of wish I took a shot at him."

The hit left Murray motionless on the field at U.S. Bank Stadium, and players later confirmed that his body was in a fencing posture, a common immediate reaction to brain trauma.

"Obviously somebody hit him while he was down. But as soon as that happened and I saw his reaction to that, it was really just frustration," Vikings star receiver Justin Jefferson said. "I hate to see anyone go down with an injury, especially an injury like that. For our starting quarterback to go down that early in that way, it was definitely very tough to see."

While Murray was placed in concussion protocol, head coach Kevin O'Connell said his interactions with teammates in the post-game locker room were encouraging.

"I don't have a lot to update," O'Connell said, "other than I did just see him and he seemed to be doing pretty well."

The Vikings got the last laugh against their NFC North rivals, defeating the Packers 39-22 behind three touchdown passes from backup quarterback Carson Wentz.

While Murray recovers, Wentz will likely be under center again when the Vikings return to action in Week 2 in another NFC North matchup against the Chicago Bears (1-0).

articles.title: Week 2 Fantasy Football Rankings, Projections and Waiver-Wire Tips
articles.summary: Week 1 of the 2026 NFL season has already brought about monster performances, colossal disappointments and everything in between.
articles.body:
Week 1 of the 2026 NFL season has already brought about monster performances, colossal disappointments and everything in between.

We aren't here to reflect on what's happened, though. Because in the world of fantasy football, it's all about looking forward.

To help you do exactly that, we'll lay out our Week 2 rankings at the marquee positions, along with waiver-wire targets (and projections for them) at each spot.

Waiver-wire target: Tyler Shough, NO (at BAL)

Volume is a coveted commodity on the waiver wire, and few passers will exit Week 1 offering more than Shough. He was active early and often in New Orleans' overtime loss to Detroit, hoisting 56 throws and connecting on 35 of them for 410 yards and three touchdowns. He wasn't super efficient (two interceptions and five sacks), but with volume like this, he may not have to be.

Projected stats: 27-of-40 for 278 yards, two touchdowns, one interception

Waiver-wire target: Kaelon Black, SF (vs. MIA)

Black might be optimized as a McCaffrey handcuff, but given San Francisco's apparent intent to lighten the veteran's workload, Black might have legitimate standalone value. Especially in a favorable matchup that could have the Niners up big early. The rookie third-rounder had 14 carries for 65 yards and a five-yard reception in San Francisco's season-opener.

Projected stats: 13 carries for 71 yards and one touchdown, two receptions for 13 yards

Waiver-wire target: Devaughn Vele, NO (at BAL)

This Saints' passing offense looks like one you'll want exposure to, and it should make Vele a priority target this week. He saw nine targets on Sunday and turned them into seven receptions for 69 yards and a score. With Jordyn Tyson on injured reserve, Vele is positioned to make some early noise as the No. 2 receiver.

Projected stats: Six receptions for 71 yards and one touchdown

articles.title: 'Whatever It Takes,' Patrick Mahomes' Return from Injury Detailed Before Chiefs' Opener vs. Broncos
articles.summary: Kansas City Chiefs star Patrick Mahomes had one clear mission statement as he worked his way back from a torn ACL and LCL.
articles.body:
Kansas City Chiefs star Patrick Mahomes had one clear mission statement as he worked his way back from a torn ACL and LCL.

According to ESPN's Nate Taylor , that was the message Mahomes relayed to Dr. Dan Cooper, the Dallas Cowboys head team physician, after Cooper told him he needed to be in Dallas the next day for surgery.

"Throughout his rehab and recovery, Mahomes has said that same sentence many different times," Taylor wrote. "And his exhaustive, day-after-day actions have led to him achieving his mission — one that began next to the MRI machine 274 days ago."

The six-time Pro Bowler went down in a loss to the Los Angeles Chargers on Dec. 14. He had knee surgery on Dec. 15.

"The toughest part was the beginning, not being able to get up and chase my kids around," Mahomes told Taylor of the overall process. "I remember sitting at the [training] table and watching us play those last few [road] games and how much it hurt me."

Chiefs tight end Travis Kelce relayed to The Athletic's Jesse Newell how Mahomes "flipped a switch from the moment he had that surgery."

"He had a goal in mind to be able to be here Week 1 with us. And he's here," Kelce said.

Head coach Andy Reid echoed a similar sentiment, telling Newell that "there was no hesitation" when Mahomes set a goal of playing in Week 1.

"There were no days off," Reid said. "He kept stacking the days. Some days you don't want to go in there. You're not feeling it. But he kept showing up."

Mahomes was already a leader inside the Kansas City locker room. His recovery provided another way for him to set the tone internally.

"The level of sacrifice is something that has been an example throughout the entire organization," general manager Brett Veach said.

According to Taylor, Mahomes started rehabbing daily at the Chiefs' facility in January and would often spend seven-plus hours there. He worked with assistant athletic trainer Julie Frymyer to assess his recovery by two-week increments, and they relayed his results to Cooper.

Taylor provided the details behind a March video posted by Mahomes, which started to get fans seriously excited about the idea he'd suit up in Week 1.

The veteran quarterback and personal trainer Bobby Stroupe threw a baseball back and forth, which was a "spontaneous moment" because some baseball players were working out at the same location. Later on, Stroupe tossed a football to Mahomes and used Mahomes' phone to record a short clip of the QB going through his usual motions on a throw.

While Mahomes clearly wasn't going at full speed, the video was an encouraging sign of how much his knee had healed.

During his long road back, the two-time NFL MVP got help from an unexpected source.

Veteran tight end Zach Ertz told Newell last month he reached out to Mahomes as soon as he saw the Chiefs star go down. Ertz tore his ACL a week earlier, so he understood the position Mahomes was soon to find himself in.

The two built a friendship and used each other as a source of motivation.

"It would start off as, 'What are you deadlifting?'" Mahomes said to Taylor. "Then it's like sending little videos. He's jumping and doing certain acceleration things. I'm sending him [the] next week [me] doing cutting and stuff like that.

"Sometimes you're lonely because you're doing stuff by yourself. It gave me someone else that I can compete with to kind of push my competitive drive."

The Chiefs didn't give Mahomes an injury designation heading into their opener against the Denver Broncos. That set the stage for him to resume his usual starting role.

Nobody knows for sure how he'll fare once the game begins, though.

Mahomes hinted at one small adjustment he could make after his knee injury. He told Taylor that he "ran a little bit too much" toward the end of his 2025 season.

Mahomes' ability to improvise in the pocket is a a reason why he has been so successful in the NFL. That may be a facet of his game he curtails a bit to limit the hits he's taking.

In general, nobody is doubting whether he'll remain an elite passer given how aggressively he worked to get ready for Week 1.

articles.title: Chris Olave Explains Decision to Change Helmet to Guardian Cap in Saints' NFL Opener vs. Lions
articles.summary: New Orleans Saints wide receiver Chris Olave was seen wearing a Guardian Cap in Sunday's season opener against the Detroit Lions, and he explained after the game why he switched from his regular helmet.
articles.body:
New Orleans Saints wide receiver Chris Olave was seen wearing a Guardian Cap in Sunday's season opener against the Detroit Lions, and he explained after the game why he switched from his regular helmet.

"I know all the head injuries I've had in my career, so it was just a decision I had made. I got kids now, I want to be able to live the long game, it's not all about football," Olave told reporters. "I want to live regular life after I'm done with football, I love my kids to death. I don't really care how it looks no more, I just gotta throw it on. Shoot, it did me good today, for sure."

Watch: NFL player arrives wearing Spiderman costume

Olave didn't appear hindered at all by the Guardian Cap, as he tied for the game-high with 10 catches and set a new career-high with 182 receiving yards in Sunday's season opener. Despite his individual dominance, the Saints suffered a 31-30 loss to the Lions in overtime. Still, it was an encouraging performance for a rebuilding New Orleans team, as second-year quarterback Tyler Shough threw for 410 yards, three touchdowns and two interceptions.

Per Fox Sports , Olave had suffered a concussion in three straight seasons from 2022 to 2024. He suffered two in 2024 that limited him to just eight games. In total, he's suffered four concussions in his professional career and five since starting college.

Despite his injury history, Olave is a franchise cornerstone for the Saints. The team signed him to a four-year, $132 million contract extension in July, rewarding him after he finished the 2025 season with career highs of 100 catches, 1,163 yards and nine touchdowns.

Olave's season-opening performance showed that he's ready to pick up right where he left off, and he will have a better chance at staying healthy while he wears the Guardian Cap.

Olave and the Saints will try to earn their first win of the year in Week 2 when they face the Baltimore Ravens (1-0) next Sunday.

articles.title: Jacoby Brissett Calls Out Fantasy Players About Kendrick Bourne and Hypes Jeremiyah Love
articles.summary: Arizona Cardinals quarterback Jacoby Brissett knew a big game from wide receiver Kendrick Bourne wasn't what a lot of fantasy football managers had planned in Week 1.
articles.body:
Arizona Cardinals quarterback Jacoby Brissett knew a big game from wide receiver Kendrick Bourne wasn't what a lot of fantasy football managers had planned in Week 1.

"I'm pretty sure none of y'all had him on your fantasy (team)," Brissett said in his postgame press conference. "He was just in the right spot at the right time on a lot of plays. We put him there because we trust him there."

Bourne caught eight passes for 75 yards as Arizona upset the Los Angeles Chargers 26-14.

Rookie running back Jeremiyah Love was equal parts encouraging and frustrating. He finished with 41 rushing yards and a touchdown but had six fewer carries than Tyler Allgeier.

Regardless of his usage, Brissett believes Love is a special talent in the backfield.

Overreactions are inevitable after Week 1. Teams are never the finished product in their first game.

The Cardinals may have encountered the Chargers, a contender with big ambitions, at the perfect time. Or perhaps Arizona was underestimated coming into the year.

Brissett demonstrated why he won the starting job by going 27-of-37 for 277 yards and one touchdown. Thanks to the efforts of Love and Allgeier, the offense gained 116 yards on the ground. And the defense forced two turnovers while limiting Chargers quarterback Justin Herbert to 209 yards through the air.

In the case of Brissett, there's a reason he has bounced around the NFL the last few years and failed to be a full-time starter permanently. His steady hand should at least keep the Cardinals on track as they continue to figure out their long-term direction.

Even if Arizona winds up with a losing record when all is said and done, the team can provide signs under first-year coach Mike LaFleur to generate optimism about 2027 and beyond.

articles.title: Tyreek Hill Says 'NFL Twitter Has Me in Tears' After Missing Opening Day Due to Injury
articles.summary: Veteran wider receiver Tyreek Hill remains a free agent while recovering from a devastating knee injury, but he appears to be enjoying his time off the field.
articles.body:
Veteran wider receiver Tyreek Hill remains a free agent while recovering from a devastating knee injury, but he appears to be enjoying his time off the field.

Hill took to social media while watching the Week 1 slate for the 2026 season, and he said the posts from fans on NFL Twitter has him "in tears."

Hill, who last played for the Miami Dolphins, is recovering from major surgery to repair his dislocated left knee and multiple torn ligaments, including his ACL.

While it's safe to say that the eight-time Pro Bowler would prefer to be on the field, it appears that he has enough to keep him entertained during his time away.

articles.title: Broncos vs. Chiefs Monday Night Football betting odds, picks and predictions: Best bets, player props
articles.summary: Our NFL handicapper break downs his favorite bets in the Broncos-Chiefs Monday Night Football matchup.
articles.body:
Week 1 wraps up with maybe its most high-leverage matchup, as the long-time AFC West super-power ( Kansas City ) takes on last season's division champ ( Denver ) — the only matchup between the top-two choices in a divisional betting market (especially after the Chargers were upset on Sunday).

That Patrick Mahomes is returning from a knee injury which put the final nail in the Chiefs ' 2025 season adds some intrigue against a Broncos team that might have been an injury to their own quarterback away from making the Super Bo wl.

Despite Kansas City's down year, and Denver's status as the No. 1 seed in the AFC last season, the betting market is still favoring the Chiefs, even before a couple points have been applied for a Monday night in Arrowhead.

Denver Broncos at Kansas City Chiefs (-2.5, 43.5)

Let's start with a low-level anthropological study of sharp sports bettors.

If at any point after this line opened in mid-May, you officially decided to bet on the Broncos, and saw the line at +2.5, so close to the key number of +3, with a popular team known to take money like the Chiefs, why wouldn't you wait all summer long to see if bookmakers felt compelled to bump it up to +3?

It's entirely possible that we're all sitting around waiting to make a bet on the Broncos at the best number available, and if we're all trying to be patient, then there isn't enough Denver money coming in to move this game closer to pick-em.

On the field, if any quarterback is coming back from a significant knee injury (or even if one that isn't), you might expect the betting market would think it's crucial that his blindside is adequately protected. Yet, last week's news of left tackle Josh Simmons being out for Monday night, with a rookie starting in his place, still didn't trigger a move towards the Broncos. Again, potentially, because we're all waiting for +3.

Well, hours before kickoff, we're running low on time.

When Mahomes went down last season, the Chiefs weren't better than the Broncos. And with a defensive front that can take advantage of Simmons' absence and stuff Kansas City's alleged commitment to a run game with Kenneth Walker , Kansas City isn't better than Denver now.

If this game doesn't drift down to pick-em by kickoff, I'll be surprised, as that would be a mistake.

WR Jaylen Waddle over 52.5 receiving yards (-115, Bet365)

We didn't mention the matchup of the Broncos' offense against the Chiefs defense, because we were saving that handicap for our player prop section. Denver made a point to go out and get Jaylen Waddle, and I'll be shocked if Sean Payton doesn't make a point to use him constantly this season to take even more pressure off of Bo Nix.

Two quality corners went from the Chiefs to the Rams in the offseason, and that's probably a necessary move in the long term for Kansas City to manage its salary cap. However, hoping first-round pick Mansoor Delane plays at a high level from Game 1, and that L'Jarius Sneed turns back the clock the second time around in K.C. seems perilous in a tough matchup. Especially, with a pass-rush mitigated by one of the best offensive lines in the league.

QB Patrick Mahomes under 229.5 passing yards (-115, Bet365)

Here's a derivative way to play on a shaky performance from Mahomes, coming off of injury and with a rookie protecting his blind side. Also, the Chiefs still haven't answered a lack of explosiveness and depth in their receiving corps, and Patrick Surtain II should have his usual one-half of the field locked down.

RB Brashard Smith over 12.5 rushing + receiving yards (-115, Bet365)

Through thick-and-thin last season, Brashard Smith was a pet props project of ours over at THE WINDOW, as a quasi-gadget player out of the Chiefs' backfield, capable of turning a few touches into big plays.

Before Mahomes' injury, Smith had at least three touches in a six-of-seven game stretch. In this second season, more should be on Smith's plate for an offense that he was added to late in the 2025 draft because it has lacked explosiveness.

See above, for why Waddle will be a part of the overall game plan, as his speed allows for a possible short throw that turns into a long gain.

Engram scored just one touchdown in his first season with the Broncos, despite 50 catches in the regular season on 76 targets. In 2024, all Denver tight ends combined had 51 receptions on 70 targets, but they had five touchdowns in Payton's offense.

With the assumption of at least the usual workload in this role, we should expect an Engram touchdown around a quarter of the time, making fair odds closer to +300.

Rice came off suspension last season, and was immediately a red-zone weapon, with two touchdowns on quick tosses designed for him. With six touchdowns overall, Rice scored in half his eight games played in 2025, after scoring in two of four games played in 2024. Scoring 50% of the time implies even-money odds, so anything better than +150 is worth a look, even on the side we're against for the game as a whole.

You can find more valuable betting analysis from Yahoo Sports betting contributor, Matt Russell , at THE WINDOW .

articles.title: Deshaun Watson 'Widely Seen' Within Browns as 'Best' QB Over Shedeur Sanders, New NFL Rumors Reveal
articles.summary: Despite Cleveland Browns veteran quarterback Deshaun Watson's struggles in Sunday's season opener against the Jacksonville Jaguars, he reportedly hasn't fallen out of favor with the organization.
articles.body:
Despite Cleveland Browns veteran quarterback Deshaun Watson's struggles in Sunday's season opener against the Jacksonville Jaguars, he reportedly hasn't fallen out of favor with the organization.

Albert Breer of Sports Illustrated reported that Watson is "widely seen internally as the best option" for the Browns over backup quarterback Shedeur Sanders.

Watson threw an interception on the fifth play of the game and finished with just 205 yards and a garbage-time touchdown in Cleveland's 34-10 loss to Jacksonville. Fans on social media panned his performance in the first half and called for Sanders to replace him after just one game.

According to Breer, Browns first-year head coach Todd Monken tabbed Watson as Cleveland's starting quarterback while "knowing that it'd be much easier to pull the plug on him and go to Sanders than to do the opposite." Breer added that Monken "did leave open the possibility that a change would come in-season."

Watson accepted responsibility for Cleveland's poor offensive performance, and he expressed confidence that he would be better in Week 2 against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.

"We left a lot out there, so obviously, I'll take that responsibility full throttle," he told reporters . "We gotta look at the tape and see how we can be better and try to attack Tampa Bay next week to be able to get points on the board to be able to get a win."

Still, it can be expected that any further struggles by Watson will only make the calls for Sanders grow louder as the Browns go through a tough early-season slate.

articles.title: Sports Scientists React to McVay, Rams' Travel Plan to Australia After Myles Garrett's Injury, Loss
articles.summary: The Los Angeles Rams' travel strategy for their opening game may draw additional scrutiny in the wake of Myles Garrett's knee injury.
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Rams' travel strategy for their opening game may draw additional scrutiny in the wake of Myles Garrett's knee injury.

The Ringer's Tom Pelissero reported the reigning Defensive Player of the Year will undergo arthroscopic surgery and go on injured reserve, sidelining him for a minimum of four games.

Mike Sando of The Athletic detailed one possible downside to the Rams arriving in Australia a little over day before their game against the San Francisco 49ers.

"Sports scientists I spoke with said the Rams were spot-on in their handling of the sleep component, but they risked players feeling heavy-legged because it takes time for fluid buildup in the legs to dissipate following such a long flight," Sando wrote. "The problem can be exacerbated for bigger players like Garrett, who for the first time in his career played at least 55 snaps without recording even one tackle."

The Rams came out flat and lost 27-7 to San Francisco, and Garrett had a debut to forget.

The seven-time Pro Bowler told reporters after the defeat that "I didn't feel I was the player I've been before when I stepped on the field."

His critical assessment raised some concerns in the view of one former Cleveland Browns assistant.

"When Myles said he needed to change and do whatever he needed to get himself ready, I took that as either he did not buy into what the team was doing, or there was another ailment going on," they said to Sando. "It was probably a little bit of both."

It's not as though the Rams were the first Super Bowl contender to ever lay an egg in Week 1. Drake Maye threw three interceptions in the New England Patriots' 13-10 loss to the Seattle Seahawks, who dropped their 2025 opener en route to winning a title.

Given the outcome, Los Angeles nevertheless may have taken a more traditional approach to its long journey to Australia with the benefit of hindsight.

articles.title: Trevor Lawrence Reacts to Not Getting the Ball from His 100th Jaguars TD Pass in Trending Video
articles.summary: Jacksonville Jaguars star quarterback Trevor Lawrence threw his 100th touchdown pass in Sunday's 34-10 win over the Cleveland Browns, but he wasn't able to comemorate the moment.
articles.body:
Jacksonville Jaguars star quarterback Trevor Lawrence threw his 100th touchdown pass in Sunday's 34-10 win over the Cleveland Browns, but he wasn't able to comemorate the moment.

Lawrence told reporters that rookie wide receiver Josh Cameron was given the ball after recording his first touchdown reception. The 26-year-old didn't realize it was his 100th touchdown pass until someone informed him in the locker room.

"I'm like, 'Oh, where's that ball?' and they're like, 'It was Josh's first one.' So, he can keep it," Lawrence said. "I guess I gotta go get 200 now. I'll keep that one."

Lawrence threw four touchdown passes to four different receivers in the blowout victory on Sunday.

Lawrence will continue the march to 200 touchdown passes when the Jags return to action in Week 2 against the Denver Broncos.

articles.title: Lamar Jackson Hypes Ravens' New OC, 'His Mind Is Out of This World' After Blowout Win vs. Colts
articles.summary: Lamar Jackson is a pretty big fan of new offensive coordinator Declan Doyle.
articles.body:
Lamar Jackson is a pretty big fan of new offensive coordinator Declan Doyle.

"It's just the same thing, overemphasizing the details," the Baltimore Ravens superstar quarterback told Albert Breer of SI.com regarding Doyle. "You want us to be detailed out, within the play. 'Guys, make sure you're doing this with your steps, so the timing of throws, runs, all of it can conjoin at the same time.' His mind is out of his world, man. Shouts out to Dec again."

Jackson threw for 324 yards and a touchdown and ran for 40 yards and a score during Sunday's 41–23 dismantling of the Indianapolis Colts, so it isn't a surprise that he was pleased with the game plan from Doyle and new head coach Mike Minter.

"I mean, I'm extremely excited," he told Breer. "But it's only the first game, so I'm not trying to get ahead of myself and the team is not trying to get ahead of [itself]. We're just trying to stay locked in, dialed in with the details. Like I've been saying this whole time, started off in OTAs, the whole offseason program. Declan was already on us, 'Hey, do this and that,' and that, just, like I said, detailed. Same thing with Jesse."

articles.title: QB Report Cards for 2026 NFL Week 1
articles.summary: Typically, the start of a new NFL season sets the bar for expectations, specifically the quarterback position. The lineup for Week 1 serves as the preview of how a team is supposed to look throughout the campaign and who will be leading the group. The 2027 already looks different after one game.
articles.body:
Typically, the start of a new NFL season sets the bar for expectations, specifically the quarterback position. The lineup for Week 1 serves as the preview of how a team is supposed to look throughout the campaign and who will be leading the group. The 2027 already looks different after one game.

The reigning Super Bowl champions, the Seattle Seahawks, will be without Sam Darnold for a "couple games" due to a glute injury, according to NFL Network's Ian Rapoport . In the same opener, life became far more difficult for the New England Patriots' Drake Maye since his top target, AJ Brown, has been placed on injured reserve with an expectation of missing at least six weeks. Kyler Murray began the season as the Minnesota Vikings' quarterback but suffered a concussion and didn't finish his debut with the team. The Atlanta Falcons didn't even make it to Week 1 before they were down to QB3 upon facing the Pittsburgh Steelers. Each week, Bleacher Report will grade every quarterback performance no matter how their play shakes out throughout the action.

Score : 26-14 win vs. Los Angeles Chargers

Stat Line : 27 of 37 for 277 yards and a touchdown

The Cardinals were written off by everyone outside of their building before the 2026 campaign began. Arizona's locker room wasn't ready to concede the season, though. In the most surprising outcome of the opening weekend, the Cardinals handled the Los Angeles Chargers.

Last season, Jacoby Brissett posted impressive passing statistics, albeit in losing efforts. On Sunday, the veteran quarterback operated Mike LaFleur's system efficiently for the most part, expect for an ill-advised, late second-quarter heave that was nearly intercepted near the goal line.

Otherwise, the Cardinals coaching staff placed Brissett and the offense in a position to succeed, as the group accumulated 393 yards.

"[Coach LaFleur] was great today," Brissett said in a postgame interview with CBS' Melanie Collins . "Me and him, I felt like we were in-synch from Play 1."

Score : 20-13 loss vs. Pittsburgh Steelers

Stat Line : 12 of 22 for 143 yards, one touchdown and two interceptions

The Falcons placed Cooper Rush in a near-impossible situation. Neither of Atlanta's top-two quarterbacks were able to play Sunday against the Pittsburgh Steelers. Thus, it fell on the squad's QB3 to open the season as the Falcons' starter.

To make matter worse, Rush suffered from back spasms leading into the contest. Now, go face the Steelers defense. Good luck.

Still, the Falcons feature significant offensive skill talent. But Rush and Co. couldn't get the passing game off the ground. In fact, the team's wide receivers caught only three passes. The majority of Rush's 12 completions went to running back Bijan Robinson. The quarterback targeted tight end Kyle Pitts only once.

It's' difficult to give Rush a failing grade because of extenuating circumstances. At the same time, he didn't play well.

Score : 41-23 win vs. Indianapolis Colts

Stat Line : 17 of 25 for 324 yards, a touchdown and a fumble lost; seven carries for 40 yards a score

A different version of Lamar Jackson showed up Sunday against the Indianapolis Colts. No, he's still as much of a playmaker as he's been throughout in his career. In this case, the dual-threat quarterback's deployment was different.

As noted by Sumer Sports' Shawn Syed , Jackson posted the highest career percentages working from under center and dropping back from center. Jackson and Co. shredded the Colts defense and amassed 506 yards. Baltimore basically did whatever it wanted, with Jackson leading the way.

As this offense continues to evolve under the supervision of coordinator Declan Doyle, the quarterback's usage will be watched closely. Initial returns are quite promising, though.

"It's just football at the end of the day," Jackson said during an postgame interview with CBS Sports' AJ Ross . "But you know we've been preparing, been prepping. Coach Declan's been out of this world when it comes to details."

Stat Line : 20 of 29 for 334 yards and two touchdowns; six carries for 23 yards and two scores

The Houston Texans lacked kryptonite and shouldn't have pulled on Superman's cape. Instead, Josh Allen once again proved to be the standard at quarterback due to his combination of size, arm strength, mobility and playmaking ability.

Allen scored a pair of rushing touchdowns. The Bills were trailing in both instances. After the Texans secured a late fourth-quarter lead, Buffalo's quarterback led a seven-play, 96-yard scoring drive against the game's best defense. Ultimately, Allen connected on a 34-yard pass to Josh Palmer. Interestingly, Allen executed the play despite it not being by design.

"You want the absolute truth?" Allen said during a postgame interview with CBS Sports' Evan Washburn . "We call this a horseshoe. That wasn't where the ball was supposed to go. We have never once repped the ball going there. I just felt those safeties started cheating toward DJ (Moore) a little bit. Josh ran a great route. I put in on a line for him and he did the rest."

Stat Line : 23 of 37 for 361 yards, three touchdowns and an interception; two carries, 10 yards and a score

The version of Bryce Young that showed up Sunday will finally validate the the Panthers' decision to select him with the No. 1 overall pick in the 2023 NFL draft. Young had his moments during his previous three seasons, but he hasn't consistently looked like a true franchise quarterback. During Sunday's action, the Panthers quarterback went punch for punch with Caleb Williams and the Bears' high-flying offense. Young looked comfortable and made some outstanding throws, sans an interception due to the defensive back undercutting an out pattern.

"Every game, I'm impressed by him," wide receiver Jalen Coker said of Young . "He's a dog. Gritty. Throwing on the run. I cannot say enough good things about him. Unfortunately, Young and the Panthers offense didn't receive any help from Carolina's defense, which marred an outstanding performance.

Stat Line : 21 of 29 for 269 yards and two touchdowns; 10 carries for 65 yards and two scores

The Bears offense is already humming to the tune of 552 yards in the team's season-opener against the Carolina Panthers. Chicago's 59 points were a franchise-best in a season-opener. For context, the Bears organization has existed since 1920.

Caleb Williams continues to grow in Ben Johnson's offensive scheme without limiting his natural playmaking prowess. In fact, the opposite is happening. Williams is expanding an already proven offensive system and making it more dynamic.

The 2024 first overall draft pick can drop an impressive opposite-hash dime between two defenders to tight end Cole Kmet between for a score, while also scampering for a pair of touchdowns in the same contest.

Williams is maturing into his final form.

"I could kind of tell [Saturday] night, we were doing our quarterback meeting one last time, and I mean, he was on top of it," Johnson said after the game . "Everything he was rattling out, just where (his) eyes need to be, what (he's) thinking. I slept really well with that in mind."

Score : 33-27 win vs. Tampa Bay Buccaneers

Stat Line : 25 of 35 for 254 yards, a touchdown and an interception; five carries for 20 yards

Joe Burrow wasn't perfect against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, but he was definitely good enough for Cincinnati to accumulate 351 yards and score on six of its nine drives, including the final series to run out the clock.

Technically, Burrow led seven scoring drives. The quarterback helped Tampa Bay score a touchdown when he threw a pick-six to rookie linebacker Josiah Trotter.

"Terrible. Terrible from me," Burrow told reporters. "Y'know, I had an out-route to the field. The defender got underneath it. I tried to throw to the replacement, and the guy made a good play. I can't make that throw."

Those types of mistakes aren't typical. Usually, Burrow displays tremendous touch and accuracy. The quarterback still spread the ball around, with nine different receivers catching passes and none with more than five grabs.

Score : 34-10 loss vs. Jacksonville Jaguars

Stat Line : 16 of 22 for 205 yards, a touchdown and an interception; six carries for 38 yards

The sentiment within the Cleveland Browns fanbase is one of complete dismay, with no hope of this season being productive. The reason is simple: Deshaun Watson shouldn't be the franchise's starting quarterback. His performance Sunday showed exactly why.

Watson looked uncomfortable in the team's offense. He had no feel for the pocket, which made life so much harder on a brand new offensive line.

The decision to start Watson already felt out of place and forced due to the circumstances of him still being on the roster. The Browns simply need to get past the previous trade and terrible contract extension. They're sunk cost. The organization must move forward with someone else behind center. Otherwise, Watson's status will be the primary discussion point each and every week.

"I'm sure as hell not firing me. I'm not firing our staff. I'm not getting rid of all our players. He happens to be one of 53," head coach Todd Monken said when asked about whether Watson will start in Week 2. "So, we'll evaluate everything. We just didn't play good enough...didn't coach well enough."

Stat Line : 22 of 34 for 175 yards, two touchdowns and an interception

The Cowboys offense was supposed to be difficult to stop this season. The team was supposed to get help from a much-improved defense. Neither proved to be true during Dallas' season-opener against the New York Giants.

To make matters worse, quarterback Dak Prescott has been the team's most reliable performer. However, the game turned late in the second quarter when Prescott attempted to throw away a pass only for Giants safety Jevón Holland to grab the interception. Six plays later, New York scored a touchdown and never looked back.

"That was crucial," Prescott told reporters . "I was trying to throw the ball away. The guy made a hell of a play. I got to make sure that it's out of bounds, though. I was surprised. It's one I want back, obviously. I think that was a huge point in the game."

Score : 31-30 win vs. New Orleans Saints

Stat Line : 26 of 39 for 206 yards and two touchdowns

Jared Goff's and the Lions' performance would have looked rather different if not for a rules quirk where a fumble/lateral somehow didn't equate to a turnover.

The New Orleans Saints could have built first-half momentum with a scoop-and-score that was called back instead of waiting until the second half before they came roaring back from a 21-point deficit.

Now, everybody knows that a fumble isn't a fumble if a quarterback intends to throw the ball forward after starting his throwing motion. [Insert confused GIF .]

Anyhow, Goff led a 10-play, 70-yard drive in overtime, where he completed five of six passes, including the game-winning score.

"We just weren't shooting ourselves in the foot," Goff said of Detroit's final offensive possession . "Positive play after positive play, staying ahead of the chains, getting in third-and-short. … When we stay on track, we score points."

Score : 39-22 loss vs. Minnesota Vikings

Stat Line : 21 of 42 for 387 yards, two touchdowns, an interception and a fumble lost

Jordan Love had the unenviable task of facing Brian Flores' defense in Week 1. Everyone knows what they're going to get against Flores scheme and it's a lot of pressure.

According to NFL Next Gen Stats (h/t Benjamin Solak ), the Minnesota Vikings blitzed Love on 78.2 percent of his dropbacks, which created a 58.2 pressure rate. Minnesota sacked Green Bay's signal-caller four times and hit him 15 more times.

Pressure will rattle any quarterback. Love still delivered in multiple instances. However, he was forced into mistakes as well. The quarterback's interception was a direct result of him throwing off his back foot and behind his receiver because pressure had affected him.

"There were a couple of plays I wish I could get back," Love told reporters . "That's part of the game. You have to find ways to overcome those. You have to handle the pressure and find answers, but that's how it is when you play this defense."

Stat Line : 26 of 38 for 274 yards, two touchdowns and two fumbles lost.

This season is built around whether CJ Stroud is actually the Houston Texans' answer at quarterback. When Josh Allen is playing in the same game, it's difficult to say Stroud is a franchise quarterback, especially with how Sunday's game ended. Stroud had his moments. He completed multiple passes of 20 or more yards and threw a pair of touchdowns. However, the turnovers became the real problem. Stroud fumbled twice. Both occurred after the quarterback tried to climb the pocket and keep his eyes downfield. Unfortunately, he didn't secure the football. The second turnover ended the game. The Texans were in scoring position with 16 seconds left to play. Though Houston did lack a timeout and the game would have likely ended with just a sack. Either way, ball security must become a priority for Stroud if the Texans plan to compete and win against the game's best teams.

Stat Line : 19 of 31 for 166 yards, a touchdown and an interception

Almost everything went wrong for the Colts after the opening series against the Baltimore Ravens. A slight silver lining may exist, though. Daniel Jones was back on the field and didn't appear drastically limited despite coming back from an Achilles tendon tear he suffered nine months ago. Clearly, the Colts' offensive coaching staff built a gameplan to ensure Jones wasn't forced to continually test the previously injured leg. The quarterback was asked to primarily line up in shotgun, get the ball out quickly and not drive it down the field. Each serves as an indication that Jones isn't 100 percent. Meanwhile, Indianapolis' defense was completely unprepared for the Ravens and allowed over 500 yards. Jones may not be what he was during the first half of the 2025 campaign, but the Colts offense can still move the ball and score some points.

Stat Line : 18 of 23 for 245 yards, 245 yards and four touchdowns

Trevor Lawrence learned how to play fast and loose last season under head coach/offensive play-caller Liam Coen. In doing so, he finally looked like the quarterback so many expected when the Jaguars chose him with the first overall pick in the 2021 NFL draft. His performance during Week 1 served as an extension of the player he has become.

Lawrence was allowed to get comfortable in the pocket and picked apart the Browns' defense. His 0.7 EPA per dropback ranked among the 98th percentile, according to Sumer Sports' Shawn Syed . The 26-year-old signal-caller spread the ball around to nine different receivers, with four different targets catching a touchdown. The Jaguars' quarterback has an opportunity to enter elite status if he continues a similar level of play in the coming weeks against the Denver Broncos, New England Patriots and Cincinnati Bengals.

Stat Line : 21 of 30 for 160 yards, three touchdowns and two interceptions

Kirk Cousins is a seat-warmer for this year's No. 1 overall draft pick, Fernando Mendoza. Any victory with Cousins at the helm is a positive as the team builds toward Mendoza's eventual first start, whenever that may be. Cousins' role until then is obvious. He needs to be efficient, particularly when operating the quick passing game, because the attack will complement Ashton Jeanty's role as the offensive focal point. Last year's sixth overall draft pick carried the ball 23 times for 102 yards and caught six passes for 45 more yards. Sunday's performance did show Cousins isn't nearly as effective when trying to drive the ball down the field. He threw two poor passes over the middle of the field that resulted in interceptions. Even so, the Raiders will take similar performances if they result in more wins than losses.

Score : 26-14 loss vs. Arizona Cardinals

Stat Line : 17 of 27 for 209 yards, a touchdown and an interception; five carries for 29 yards

The Chargers offense failed to muster much of anything in Mike McDaniel's debut as the play-caller. Los Angeles managed 268 yards. The designed run game, not including Justin Herbert's contributions, averaged 3.3 yards per carry. The passing game failed to surpass 200 yards. Plus, the rebuilt offensive line didn't hold up consistently.

Herbert only compounded the problem by trying to force matters, which led to a bad downfield interception after throwing into double coverage. Mistakes happened over and over again.

"We just have to execute … to not have penalties," Herbert told reporters . "We've got to score in the red zone. We didn't execute those third downs, and we didn't move the ball that we needed to. They played well, but it's on us to play better. It's on us to go score points, make sure that we're doing everything we can on third down in the red zone and limiting turnovers."

Score : 27-7 loss vs. San Francisco 49ers

Stat Line : 15 of 25 for 155 yards and an interception

Did everyone hear that Coyote using another Acme product to catch the Roadrunner-like thud all the way from Australia? It was the sound of all the preseason expectations placed on the Rams crashing down.

The reigning NFL MVP, Matthew Stafford, played nothing like last season. Stafford threw a touchdown pass in every season regular-season contest a year ago. He failed to do so against the San Francisco 49ers. In fact, Stafford ended the game on the bench watching his team, because the Rams played so poor for three-plus quarters.

"We didn't play well enough, obviously," Stafford told reporters . "Never got into a rhythm. Only had probably two good drives, to be honest with you, the entire day…So not enough good stuff on offense. We didn't do the things that we are accustomed to doing; that's just communicating, operating, being on the same page. Too many times we're on different pages. That starts with me. I'm the guy that's communicating all that stuff, so I've got to make sure I do a better job, make sure we're all on the same page, and we can rock and roll out there and go play the game."

Score : 27-13 loss vs. Las Vegas Raiders

Stat Line : 15 of 27 for 220 yards and an interception; six carries for 39 yards and a score The Dolphins will be fighting an uphill battle all season, because the team's roster remains the league's least talented. Quarterback Malik Willis isn't under the tutelage of Matt LaFleur with the Green Bay Packers' supporting cast anymore. Willis should be excited to serve as a starting NFL quarterback, even though he's being set up to fail. The Raiders were able to slow Miami's biggest threat, running back De'Von Achane. Third-round rookie receiver Caleb Douglas played well in his NFL debut, with game-leading 94 receiving yards. But the Dolphins lack a legitimate threat on the outside to worry opposing defenses. Willis can offset some of Miami's offensive woes thanks to his athleticism and running ability. At the same time, he will try to extend plays and run himself into pressure. The Raiders sacked Willis on five different occasions and hit him 11 more times. If things don't come together for Willis and Co., the Dolphins could easily find themselves as owners of a top three draft pick with quarterback still in question.

Stat Line : 12 of 19 for 133 yards and three touchdowns

The Vikings were ready to hand the franchise keys to Kyler Murray as their starting quarterback. Unfortunately, Murray suffered a concussion in the first quarter Sunday against the Green Bay Packers.

With Murray out of the contest, veteran Carson Wentz took over the Vikings offense and helped lead the squad to a victory. Head coach Kevin O'Connell knew exactly what to expect of Wentz if he was placed in this exact situation, hence why he was named the team's backup QB.

"Carson, he's got almost 100 career starts, what he was able to do last year from a stand point of very limited reps, but being able to apply a careers worth of experience, that's kinda what you need to do as a backup quarterback," O'Connell told reporters last week. The comment was somewhat prophetic, with Wentz leading the offense to all 39 points. The 33-year-old veteran attempted only 19 passes, but he connected on three touchdowns and didn't commit a turnover.

Stat Line : 23 of 33 for 178 yards, a touchdown and three interceptions; seven carries for 47 yards

Much like the previously discussed Matthew Stafford, Drake Maye didn't look like the MVP-caliber player seen a season ago. Instead, he three three interceptions, including the game-clinching turnover with 21 seconds left to play.

Once again, the Seattle Seahawks and head coach/defensive player-caller Mike Macdonald constructed an excellent gameplan to confuse Maye in multiple situations, as they did in Super Bowl LX. Second, the Patriots' quarterback wasn't always on the same page with his receivers. AJ Brown's injury certainly didn't help matters.

"I lost patience, and it cost us," Maye told reporters . "They were decisions that cost us the game, on my part, on my end."

Stat Line : 35 of 56 for 410 yards, three touchdowns, two interceptions and a fumble lost

Tyler Shough did everything possible to help his Saints come roaring back from a 21-point third-quarter deficit against the Detroit Lions except for make the final play in overtime to secure a victory. To the second-year quarterback's credit, he made some excellent tight-window throws and posted big numbers. He also made some poor throws from a clean pocket and committed three turnovers. The large variance seen in his game has to close where the Saints get more consistency from last year's second-year draft pick. In this particular contest, Shough played poorly during the first half then came on strong after his team was down multiple touchdowns in the second. When the Saints get a complete effort from Shough, they'll be difficult to beat.

Stat Line : 23 of 29 for 230 yards, three touchdowns; 11 carries for 54 yards

John Harbaugh's hire as the Giants' head coach was meant to stabilize the organization and provide the team with credibility. He's the same coach who helped Lamar Jackson become a two-time NFL MVP. No one is saying that Jaxson Dart is the next Lamar Jackson. However, the Giants appear to have something special in their second-year quarterback.

Dart's performance during Sunday Night Football against the rival Dallas Cowboys was nearly flawless, which portends bigger and better things for the quarterback and his team.

"For him to have all this on his plate and to execute the way he did, to me, was just tremendous and very impressive," Harbaugh told reporters . "It was a great performance by Jaxson."

Dart added, "I felt very comfortable. I thought that we just did a really good job of staying in progress throughout the game. I thought (offensive coordinator Matt Nagy) called an awesome game, and I thought the guys just played really, really hard. So it made my job a lot easier, and guys all over the place made a ton of plays, so I'm excited about that."

Stat Line : 19 of 24 for 215 yards Geno Smith deserves significant credit for stepping into the Jets' starting quarterback job and helping in the victory. A year ago, Smith was in the same position with the Las Vegas Raiders, who were looking for a veteran presence. Instead, Smith was the league's worst quarterback. The Jets' decision to trade for the 35-year-old this offseason came across as a team settling at quarterback, because the organization knew its wasn't in position to draft a top prospect. Furthermore, Smith returned to the same franchise that originally drafted him and eventually viewed him as a bust.

Ten seasons after leaving the Jets, the 2013 second-round draft pick didn't make any critical mistakes and successfully led a run-heavy, ball-control offense. The Jets ran the ball 39 times and held the ball for over 38 minutes. This formula can make New York highly competitive during Aaron Glenn's second year as head coach.

Score : 24-22 win vs. Washington Commanders

Stat Line : 14 of 25 for 203 yards and three touchdowns; seven carries for 46 yards

AJ Brown is gone, and he's not coming back to the Philadelphia Eagles. After last season's continued in-fighting and stagnant offensive effort, the Eagles and quarterback Jalen Hurts started fresh this fall.

Despite Browns' departure, Hurts was particularly effective driving the ball down the field. As Victor Williams of The Eagles Wire noted, Hurts completed six of nine passes for 176 yards and three touchdowns when attempting passes 10 or more air yards down the field.

Philadelphia's offense is built around a talented offensive line and an effective ground attack. Hurts struggled to make opponents pay off the play-action game in 2025. He looks to be back on track for the start of the current campaign.

"Jalen has worked extremely hard at that portion of his game," head coach Nick Sirianni told reporters . "He really can throw. He just puts the ball on the money in those situations, which helps you be explosive."

Stat Line : 24 of 40 for 221 yards and a touchdown

The idea of Aaron Rodgers carrying an offense is long gone. However, the league's oldest player understands the Steelers are close to clicking, even if the unit didn't quite reach that level against the Atlanta Falcons.

"We had a chance to be really, really explosive," Rodgers said during a post-game interview with FOX Sports' Pam Oliver . "We had a couple drops. A couple off targets. A couple non-calls that looked like penalties. ... We were just a little bit off." The comments allude to the small margin of error the Steelers offense will have on a weekly basis. Rodgers can get the unit into the right play and still make some precise throws. However, he needs his playmakers to consistently do their job in order for the group to maximize this season.

Stat Line : 24 of 34 for 205 yards, three touchdowns and an interception

Maybe Brock Purdy suffered from a west-coast delay before he finally realized the 49ers were ahead of schedule when playing the rival Los Angeles Rams in a different time zone.

The Niners quarterback started somewhat slowly, looking like he was just trying to get the ball out quickly and avoid the Rams' pass rush. During San Francisco's third offensive possession, Purdy completely missed a dropping Quentin Lake and threw a poor interception .

From that point, the 49ers' signal-caller completed 12 of 14 passes for 125 yards and three touchdowns. The 26-year-old veteran also quickly established a rapport with his new top target, Mike Evans, and adjusted when standout rookie De'Zhaun Stribling suffered an injury that subsequently placed him on injured reserve.

Score : 13-10 win vs. New England Patriots

Stat Line : 16 of 22 for 187 yards and a touchdown

The Seahawks enjoyed five plays with Sam Darnold behind center before the team's Super Bowl-winning starting quarterback was injured and ruled out of the game.

According to NFL Network's Ian Rapoport , Darnold suffered a glute injury, which will likely keep him out of the next game or two. Drew Lock was thrust into the lineup and did exactly what's needed of a backup quarterback unexpected called to service. He didn't lose his team the game by making significant mistakes and did enough to ensure a victory. Seattle's defense dictated the outcome, which is par for the course. But Lock played well enough for the the Seahawks not to be rattled as they prepare for the Arizona Cardinals and Washington Commanders over the next two weekends.

Score : 33-27 loss vs. Cincinnati Bengals

Stat Line : 23 of 28 for 216 yards and three lost fumbles

Baker Mayfield is whirling dervish of combustible energy when he plays the game. His approach often keeps the quarterback (and his team) on the razor's edge throughout contests.

Case in point, the Buccaneers offense moved the ball Sunday and nearly averaged the same yards per play as the Cincinnati Bengals. Three lost fumbles by the quarterback is simply inexcusable. Yes, he was trying to make plays and extend drives. Ball security must become a much higher priority.

"This one falls on me," Mayfield told reporters . "I think they had 17 points alone off my turnovers. It turned out to be a one-score game. Offensively, it's frustrating you do something like that when you're moving the ball."

Stat Line : 19 of 32 for 140 yards and a touchdown; four carries for 21 yards Cam Ward showed slow, incremental growth during his rookie campaign. Last year's No. 1 overall pick did nothing during his Year 2 opener to think he remains on that trajectory. To be fair, New York Jets head coach Robert Saleh pieced together an outstanding defensive game plan that didn't allow Ward to get into any kind of rhythm. Still, the sophomore signal-caller never looked comfortable. His lone touchdown pass came when the Titans were trailing 23-3 with under three minutes remaining. Ward made multiple poor decisions and missed throws. He finished the contest with a 34.4 QBR. For comparison, he finished with a 33.2 QBR last season. Tennessee's growth this season depends on Ward showing far more than he did during Sunday's outing.

Score : 24-22 loss vs. Philadelphia Eagles

Stat Line : 18 of 34 for 164 yards, two touchdowns; five carries for 31 yards

A healthy Jayden Daniels returning to the Washington Commanders was supposed provide the franchise with booster fuel after a disappointing 2025 campaign. Instead, Daniels and the Commanders weren't able to shift into top gear and failed to surpass the rival Philadelphia Eagles.

Daniels did get going during the fourth quarter, where he led a pair of touchdown drives and provided Washington with an opportunity to tie the game. Though the Commanders failed to convert the two-point attempt.

Despite the loss, Daniels provided promising improvement.

"It was good to see him also learn some lessons from '25—making a play, get down, throw the ball away," head coach Dan Quinn told reporters . "Those are things that, as a coach, I don't really know until we get into the games. He's such a competitor. I thought, man, it's good to have him back into this space."

articles.title: Jayden Daniels sends Stefon Diggs a clear message after goalpost celebration costs Commanders crucial points against Eagles
articles.summary: NFL News: Jayden Daniels had a clear message for Stefon Diggs after the Washington Commanders lost 24-22 to the Philadelphia Eagles. Diggs caught a fourth-quart.
articles.body: Jayden Daniels had a clear message for Stefon Diggs after the Washington Commanders lost 24-22 to the Philadelphia Eagles. Diggs caught a fourth-quarter touchdown that brought Washington within two points, but his decision to hug the goalpost after scoring brought a 15-yard unsportsmanlike conduct penalty. Daniels said the team needed to be smarter in that situation, while Diggs admitted he had made a costly mistake.Jayden Daniels calls out Stefon Diggs after costly Commanders celebrationThe Commanders were finally finding some life late in the game when Daniels connected with Diggs for a 10-yard touchdown. The score cut Philadelphia’s lead to 17-15 with 9:59 left, putting Washington in position to go for two and tie the game.Then Diggs ran toward the goalpost and jumped up to hug it.The celebration led to an unsportsmanlike conduct penalty, moving Washington back 15 yards. Instead of trying a two-point conversion from its normal spot, the Commanders had to kick the extra point. The Eagles still led 17-16, and Washington later missed a two-point attempt with 1:01 left before Philadelphia held on for the win. The Philadelphia Eagles’ official game recap confirmed that the penalty forced Washington to settle for the extra point.Daniels did not put the blame only on Diggs. The quarterback said he also should have reminded his teammates about the situation before the play.“We just have to be smart,” Daniels said. “There’s a time and place for everything and celebrations. I’m pretty sure at that point we would’ve gone for two, had to settle for the extra point.”Head coach Dan Quinn also confirmed that Washington planned to go for two before the penalty changed the situation. That made Diggs’ celebration even more frustrating because the Commanders had a chance to tie the game much earlier.Still, the penalty was not the only reason Washington lost. The Commanders eventually got another chance to tie the game, but their two-point attempt failed with just over a minute remaining. Philadelphia then recovered Washington’s onside kick attempt and finished the 24-22 win.Stefon Diggs admits he forgot the NFL goalpost celebration ruleDiggs did not try to defend what happened. Instead, the veteran receiver accepted responsibility and explained that the celebration came from an old habit.“As soon as I wrapped my arms around it, I was like, ‘Oh, I forgot,’” Diggs told reporters. “Back in the day, I’ve been playing for a long time, you used to could do that. I’ve got to be better.”Diggs’ touchdown was his first for Washington after joining the Commanders, making the celebration understandable from an emotional point of view. But the NFL no longer allows players to use the goalpost as part of a celebration, and the officials immediately flagged him for it.According to NBC Sports, Diggs said he took “full accountability” for the mistake. The report also noted that he knew almost immediately that the celebration would bring a penalty.For Daniels, the bigger lesson was about knowing the game situation. Washington was chasing a two-point deficit against the defending NFC champions, so every decision mattered.Daniels also made it clear that he was willing to share responsibility rather than simply blame his new receiver.“We gotta know situations, situational football,” Daniels said. “That’s on me for not reiterating that in the huddle.”The Commanders now turn their attention to Week 2, when Daniels and Washington will face the Dallas Cowboys. After such a narrow opening-day loss, the Diggs penalty will be one of the moments the team will want to handle better next time.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.
