articles.title: Jared Goff Reacts to Tyler Shough's Saints Going for It in OT Loss, Would Lions Have Done It?
articles.summary: The New Orleans Saints raised some eyebrows on Sunday went they went for two after scoring a touchdown on the second possession of overtime with just 1:34 remaining on the clock.
articles.body:
The New Orleans Saints raised some eyebrows on Sunday went they went for two after scoring a touchdown on the second possession of overtime with just 1:34 remaining on the clock.

Tyler Shough's pass into the corner for Bryce Lance was incomplete, giving the Detroit Lions a dramatic 31-30 win. But even the Lions thought it was the right call.

"I think you've got to go for it," quarterback Jared Goff told The Athletic's Mike Silver . "We would have done the same thing."

Given that the Lions scored on four of their seven drives between the second half and overtime—and would have only needed a field goal to win had the Saints gone for the tie—taking the risk to go for two was understandable.

articles.title: New York Giants can make NFL playoffs with new John Harbaugh culture, says Jeff Reinebold
articles.summary: The New York Giants began their season with a divisional win over the Dallas Cowboys as they seek a return to the playoffs; listen to Inside the Huddle podcast throughout the season as Neil Reynolds, Phoebe Schecter and Jeff Reinebold discuss the biggest storylines
articles.body:
Harbaugh took the reins on a coasting Giants organisation earlier this year after parting from the Baltimore Ravens following 18 seasons as head coach.

Awaiting him was a team of young talent seeking direction after just two winning seasons in the last 10 years, with Jaxson Dart inspiring fresh hope at quarterback alongside a pass rush tipped to join the league's elite units.

The first sign of Harbaugh's impact came in week one as the Giants beat their divisional rival Cowboys 28-20 after three touchdown passes from Dart, two of which went to Isaiah Likely, and a rushing score from Cam Skattebo.

"You're going to see the Harbaugh stamp on these Giants," Reinebold said on Inside the Huddle podcast. "The Giants in the last three or four years have been getting better, incrementally better.

"Harbaugh's staff didn't draft Jaxson Dart, they didn't draft Cam Skattebo, they didn't draft Malik Nabers. There's a bunch of good players in New York that they didn't draft.

"But what Harbaugh has done is he has created a culture in New York that's been lacking. Now you continue to build your roster as they have, and bringing in Isaiah Likely was a good move. If you're a Giants fan, you've got to really like the direction that this thing is going.

"It's not perfect yet. I don't think they're going to win their division. I do think they could be a playoff team."

An electric MetLife Stadium crowd would be treated to a hungry and driven team desperate to shake off the disfunctional cobwebs of predeceasing Giants outfits.

It marked their first week one home victory since 2010 and their first opening weekend win since 2022. Next up is a road trip to face the Los Angeles Rams following their loss to the San Francisco 49ers in Melbourne.

The Giants last reached the playoffs in the 2022 season when they finished third in the NFC East before beating the Minnesota Vikings on Wild Card weekend and eventually suffering a 38-7 loss to the Philadelphia Eagles in the divisional round.

"What you see is a tougher team," Reinebold continued. "You see a team that plays with emotion, that the team that plays together.

"This will be the interesting, acid test to me. In the city with the most distractions in the world, the most newspaper outlets, the most media, can he keep them focused?

"They're just out of training camp. Now they're going out last night and everybody in New York is telling them how great they are.

"Can you keep them focused over the season? They're going to have to be if they're going to be a playoff team. That's going to be Harbaugh's test."

Watch the 2026 NFL season live on Sky Sports, including every minute of the playoffs and Super Bowl LXI on Sunday February 14, 2027.

articles.title: Jason Kelce Calls Out Fans After Video Goes Viral of Chargers' OL Giving Up Sack on Justin Herbert
articles.summary: A highlight of two Arizona Cardinals sacking Justin Herbert—while three Los Angeles Chargers offensive linemen block one player—went viral following Sunday's 26-14 win for the Cardinals.
articles.body:
A highlight of two Arizona Cardinals sacking Justin Herbert—while three Los Angeles Chargers offensive linemen block one player—went viral following Sunday's 26-14 win for the Cardinals.

But former Philadelphia Eagles center Jason Kelce didn't agree with the people online who were trashing the offensive lineman involved.

"A lot of people showing they actually have absolutely no idea how protections work or what the offensive line is responsible for on any given play," he wrote on social media .

He then further broke down how the Cardinals disguised their blitz and the ensuing chaos:

"They were blocking the five guys on the line of scrimmage to start, two of those guys dropped, the right guard applied back when his guy looped out to the tackle, the center applied left when his guy dropped," he continued . "The left guard is blocking 'his man' with the other three as a result, he could have redirected maybe a touch sooner, but the blitzers were already well past him. It's also a five-man protection, so unless Herbert pulls a crazy call out of his ass because he knows for sure this blitz is coming he's going to be hot. If the call was a sort to the left, even though the center's guy was head up on the line, which we have done, that could speed the left guard redirecting to one of the blitzers, but they still would be hot from Budda [Baker]. You could argue the left tackle should squeeze this because it's five-man protection, but again they would still be hot."

In other words, Herbert should have had a hot route ready to hit when he sensed the blitz was coming, allowing the opportunity to get rid of the ball before the blitzers reached him. But either he didn't get the ball out in time, the receiver didn't run the hot route or it simply was covered and Herbert had to take the sack rather than force the throw.

Any way you slice it, the play looked bad. But it perhaps wasn't bad for the reasons people thought, even if the team's offensive line wasn't exactly great on Sunday.

articles.title: Commanders' Tyler Owens draw praise after exceptional special teams play: 'One of the greatest football plays I've ever seen'
articles.summary: One play by Tyler Owens is going to be shown to teams by "every coach in America."
articles.body:
Washington Commanders safety Tyler Owens proved one important thing with his Week 1 performance: Sometimes, the box score lies.

If you look at Owens' stat line from Sunday, you'll note that he registered just two tackles in the team's 24-22 loss to the Philadelphia Eagles . But that doesn't tell the full story … far from it.

Owens received massive praise for a phenomenal special teams tackle, one in which he aggressively fought off multiple blockers before driving the runner into the ground for the tackle.

Future NFL Hall of Famer — and current broadcaster — JJ Watt called it "one of the greatest football plays I've ever seen."

Watt added, "Every coach in America will be showing this rep to their team this week."

But Owens wasn't done. While that one play drew attention, Owens' second tackle of the game — which also came on special teams — was equally as impressive.

This time around, Owens didn't need to run through blockers, he simply ran around them and then made a great tackle when the returner tried to put a move on.

The effort, determination and the result of both plays make it clear the box score did not do Owens justice in Week 1.

That's been the case with Owens since he joined the Commanders as an undrafted free agent in 2024. He made the team's roster and has stuck with the Commanders ever since. While he has only one start under his belt, he's made his presence felt on special teams over the years.

That was clearly on display in Week 1, and Owens is finally starting to get some recognition for it.

articles.title: B/R Experts Week 2 NFL Power Rankings
articles.summary: If there's one thing that's predictable in the NFL, it's that very few things are predictable. Week 1 of the 2026 season was no exception in that regard.
articles.body:
If there's one thing that's predictable in the NFL, it's that very few things are predictable. Week 1 of the 2026 season was no exception in that regard.

The Seattle Seahawks lost their starting quarterback in the first quarter of a Super Bowl LX rematch—and still won. Los Angeles Rams team that many were ready to crown champions before the season even started got their doors blown off Down Under. Sunday featured a shootout between contenders in Houston, a massive upset in Los Angeles and the highest scoring Sunday overall since the AFL/NFL merger.

As is so often the case, what we thought we knew about the NFL's pecking order entering the season and how it looks after one week are…not the same thing. And just as they do every week, Bleacher Report NFL analysts Gary Davenport , Kris Knox , Maurice Moton and Brent Sobleski have come together to make sense of the chaos by ranking all 32 NFL teams from worst to first.

ARI | ATL | BAL | BUF | CAR | CHI | CIN | CLE | DAL | DEN | DET | GB | HOU | IND | JAX | KC | LAC | LAR | LV | MIA | MIN | NE | NO | NYG | NYJ | PHI | PIT | SEA | SF | TB | TEN | WAS

Week 1 Result: Lost at Jacksonville 34-10

It is going to be another long season at the Factory of Sadness.

Deshaun Watson's stats weren't bad in a blowout loss to the Jaguars, but his lone touchdown throw came in garbage time and for most of the game the Browns had no vertical passing attack. That let the NFL's best run defense from a year ago tee off on running back Quinshon Judkins, who averaged less than three yards per carry.

The even bigger disappointment was a Browns defense that ranked inside the top-five last year. Sure, Myles Garrett is gone. But the Jaguars did whatever they wanted offensively in Week 1, whether it was on the ground or through the air.

It was an ugly performance all the way around. And the Browns are the NFL's worst team. Again. -- Davenport

The Miami Dolphins are exactly who everyone thought they'd be. The organization is going through a rebuilding phases trying to figure out exactly what talent will be worthy of going into next offseason as potential building blocks.

On a positive note, third-round rookie wide receiver Caleb Douglas showed up in his NFL debut with a team-leading five receptions for 94 yards. Conversely, the man throwing to Douglas, Malik Willis, will need to show more as the season progresses to ensure he's the Dolphins' starting quarterback beyond this season. Willis' athleticism makes up for some of the deficiencies found around the quarterback position. Still, the 27-year-old signal-caller must show more as a passer than what everyone saw Sunday. -- Sobleski

Week 1 Result: Lost vs. New York Jets 23-10

The Tennessee Titans offense is hard to watch in small doses, let alone for three-plus hours. Fans at Nissan Stadium rightfully booed Tennessee's offense off the field after stalled drives.

Perhaps Cam Ward's preseason struggles were a legitimate cause for concern. He didn't fare any better in a full game with starters. The second-year quarterback never settled in the pocket and misfired on several downfield passes.

Titans offensive coordinator Brian Daboll must go back to the drawing board and reduce the passing attack to short and intermediate throws until Ward finds his rhythm. -- Moton

The Atlanta Falcons are already a mess only one game into the 2026 campaign. Once again, the Falcons have significant offensive talent, just not at quarterback.

Cooper Rush was forced into the starting lineup for Atlanta's season-opener, because Tua Tagovailoa suffered a back injury and Michael Penix Jr. was not ready to take over the offense. Rush was even dealing with back spasms as late as this past Saturday.

With that setup, Atlanta's wide receivers caught four total passes against the Pittsburgh Steelers. Second-team All-Pro tight end Kyle Pitts was targeted once and didn't catch anything. Unless the Falcons somehow find consistent quarterback play, Atlanta won't be able to keep pace with opponents. -- Sobleski

Aside from a few big gains, the Indianapolis Colts offense didn't have enough explosive plays to keep pace with the Baltimore Ravens last week. As expected, coming off a torn ACL, Daniel Jones had a slow start to the season, mostly dinking and dunking his way downfield with only one rush attempt for four yards.

It may take a few weeks before we see the " Indianapolis Jones " version of the Colts' quarterback again, which may be an issue. Indianapolis risks falling into an early hole with a road matchup against the Kansas City Chiefs and a divisional battle against the Houston Texans on its schedule.

By the way, Indianapolis has allowed at least 36 points in four of its last six games. With a below-average defense, the Colts need an above-average offense to be competitive. -- Moton

Week 1 Result: Lost at Philadelphia 24-22

Sunday's road loss to the rival Eagles may well haunt the Commanders for some time—because of how Washington lost.

The Commanders showed resilience in coming back on the road from a 14-3 deficit. They were admittedly outgained in the game, but only by about 20 yards. Washington had twice as many first downs as the Eagles.

Twice in the fourth quarter, the Commanders were a two-point conversion away from tying the score. But a celebration penalty by Stefon Diggs made the first impossible, and the second came up just short.

It's not the end of the world—Washington hasn't won in Philadelphia since 2022. But two years ago, when the Commanders made it to the NFC Championship Game, this was the type of game the team found a way to win.

And with a tough schedule over the next month-plus, they needed to find a way in Week 1. -- Davenport

Over the last couple of years, it was easy to write off the New York Jets as one of the NFL's worst teams. A bit of role reversal occurred Sunday, when the Jets handled their business against an inferior team in the Tennessee Titans.

Specifically, quarterback Geno Smith deserves significant credit. He was the league's worst quarterback during the 2025 campaign. He played efficient football in his return to the Jets and didn't commit any turnovers, which is quite a feat unto itself after last season.

The formula for Aaron Glenn's team to win is obvious: Play the time of possession of game thanks to a strong ground game, hope Smith doesn't revert into bad habits and let a talented defense dictate terms. -- Sobleski

Week 1 Result: Won at Los Angeles Chargers 26-14

The Arizona Cardinals pulled off the upset of the week, and they led the Los Angeles Chargers for just about the entire game. The Cardinals aren't expected to win many games this year, but perhaps analysts have underestimated them.

But before we change our perspective on the Cardinals, let's see how they match up against the reigning champions in Week 2. Remember, the Las Vegas Raiders traveled to beat the New England Patriots in Week 1 last year and won two more games that season.

That said, don't overlook Arizona's offense. First-team All-Pro tight end Trey McBride and rookie running back Jeremiyah Love will lead an exciting young unit. -- Moton

Fans shouldn't overreact to a two-touchdown win over a Miami Dolphins team that has one of the NFL's most underwhelming rosters, especially at home. However, the Las Vegas Raiders looked more like a cohesive team than they did at almost any point last season.

It's too early to declare Klink Kubiak as Las Vegas' answer at head coach. However, his team was well-prepared for Week 1 and operated like a team that can probably pull off a few upsets in 2026. However, Kirk Cousins (2 INTs) will need to be more careful with the football to keep Las Vegas in the win column and to quiet calls for rookie Fernando Mendoza. -- Knox

The Carolina Panthers provided two unexpected outcomes from Sunday's meeting with the Chicago Bears.

First, Bryce Young went punch-for-punch with fellow No. 1 overall draft pick Caleb Williams. Young hasn't lived up to expectations during the early portion of his NFL career. More often than not, the 2023 class' top selection held back Carolina's offense. To open the 2026 campaign, Young threw for 361 yards and three touchdowns. Though he probably wants the interception back.

Second, Carolina's defense didn't come to play. Ejiro Evero's unit surrendered 552 yards and allowed the Bears to score a touchdown on their last four offensive possessions. Before that point, the game was tied 31 apiece. -- Sobleski

The New Orleans Saints showed resilience by coming back from a 21-0 third-quarter deficit against the Detroit Lions. At the same time, Kellen Moore's squad came up short in overtime and failed to finish.

Moore and his staff have done a tremendous job making the Saints a competitive squad. This time a year ago, many viewed New Orleans as having the league's least talented roster. By the end of the 2025 campaign, the Saints were pushing for a potential postseason appearance. Thus, expectations rose.

New Orleans showed it could hang with the Lions despite playing poorly early in the contest. The ability to grind out a tough win when facing adversity is the next step the Saints must take. -- Sobleski

So maybe hiring John Harbaugh was a pretty good idea.

Offensively Sunday night, New York was ruthlessly efficient. Jaxson Dart was poised and accurate. Cam Skattebo didn't have huge numbers, but he got the tough yards when he needed to. Tight end Isaiah Likely was a revelation in his first game with the team.

New York was 9-of-11 on third down. That's nuts.

The defense remains a work in progress, but it made just enough plays against one of the NFL's best offenses a year ago to win the day—and a second straight contest with the Cowboys at Met Life Stadium.

It's still too early to say the Giants are good—the Dallas defense has been awful dating back to 2025. But they were in Week 1, and we'll find out soon enough how sustainable the improvement is.

The Giants are at the Rams in Week 2. -- Davenport

Five days before the Tampa Bay Buccaneers opened their 2026 campaign, the organization and quarterback Baker Mayfield agreed to a new three-year, $165 million contract extension. Buyer's remorse would be too strong of a word after Sunday's performance, but the Bucs certainly live and die with Mayfield's drastic swings in performance.

Mayfield's desire to make a play at all costs can be a positive and negative. Against the Cincinnati Bengals, his relentless nature became a significant problem. Mayfield fumbled the ball three times, which directly led to 17 points by the Bengals. When Mayfield is on his game, he can light up an opponent. But there's always that part of him where everyone knows he's operating on the edge. -- Sobleski

Are we sure that Mike McDaniel is an offensive guru? Justin Herbert never seemed to find a rhythm, and the Los Angeles Chargers offense looked every bit as disjointed as it did under Greg Roman last season. Unfortunately, the top-tier defense we saw from L.A. in 2025 was nowhere to be found.

Maybe the Arizona Cardinals are simply far better than anyone expected. However, the version of the Chargers we saw on Sunday looked like a team that could be headed to the AFC West basement. -- Knox

Week 1 Result: Lost at New York Giants 28-20

The Dallas Cowboys spent big bucks and early picks on overhauling arguably the NFL's worst defense in the offseason.

Is there a return policy? Because the new Dallas defense looked a lot like the old Dallas defense Sunday night in New York.

The New York Giants ran the ball right at Dallas to the tune of 165 yards on the ground. Jaxson Dart's passer rating was 134.2. The Giants had 11 third down attempts in the game and converted nine of them. The Dallas offense possessed the ball all of twice (scoring touchdowns both times) in the second half because the defense just could not get off the field. New York had the ball for 36:40.

We've seen this movie before—last year. And now this week's home date with the Commanders carries sizable stakes. -- Davenport

The Green Bay Packers are missing two of last year's top players, as Micah Parsons remains on short-term IR, and running back Josh Jacobs is on the commissioner's exempt list. However, that won't make the Packers feel any better about collapsing in a very winnable game against a division rival.

The Minnesota Vikings lost Kyler Murray to a concussion early, and Green Bay built a 22-10 lead by the third quarter. However, the defense failed to contain Carson Wentz, the offensive line couldn't protect Jordan Love, and the Packers watched Minnesota pull away with 29 unanswered points.

Green Bay simply can't be a factor in the NFC North if it has many similar performances. -- Knox

Granted, it was just one game. But in Week 1, Mike McCarthy's Steelers looked a lot like Mike Tomlin's Steelers of recent seasons. Good enough to beat an inferior opponent, but not like a real threat in the AFC.

Before we go any farther, respect must be placed upon the name of T.J. Watt. Watt was a wrecking ball against the Falcons, logging two sacks and notching the first pick-six of his career. But Pittsburgh having defensive success against a third-string quarterback isn't exactly a Herculean feat.

The offense was—not great. Pittsburgh had less than 275 yards of offense against a Falcons defense that isn't scaring anyone. The Steelers managed just 58 yards on the ground and well under three yards a carry.

That may be enough to beat Atlanta. But it's not going to fly next week in New England -- Davenport

This Vikings team is going to be a threat in the NFC if it can get steady quarterback play—regardless of which signal-caller provides it.

Carson Wentz largely played the game-manager role in relief of Kyler Murray (concussion). However, he put the ball in the end zone and allowed Minnesota's defense to take over the game instead of just keeping the team in it. Of course, one impressive win won't be enough to launch the Vikings toward the top of our power rankings. -- Knox

Patrick Mahomes is set to make his return from a torn ACL on Monday night against the rival Denver Broncos. The Kansas City Chiefs will need him to be in pre-injury form if they're going to get back in the playoff mix this season.

Denver should serve as a great measuring stick for how close Kansas City is to being a playoff team in 2026. -- Knox

More often than not in recent years, the Bengals have struggled out of the gate—since 2022, the Bengals are 2-6 over the first two weeks of the season. But the Bengals put one in the win column in Week 1 this year—and how they did it may have mattered even more than the win itself.

The Cincinnati offense was held at least somewhat in check—Joe Burrow barely topped 250 passing yards with a single touchdown pass. Star receiver Ja'Marr Chase had just two catches. Fellow wideout Tee Higgins and running back Chase Brown were—OK.

No, it was Cincinnati's revamped defense that won the day against Tampa, forcing four Buccaneers turnovers, dropping Baker Mayfield four times and holding the Bucs to just 282 total yards.

It's exactly what the Bengals were looking for—a measure of balance, And in Cincy can keep playing defense like this, the Bengals are going to be a tough out. – Davenport

Week 1 Result: Won vs. New Orleans 31-30 (OT)

Drew Petzing's first game as the Detroit Lions' offensive coordinator was a whole bunch of fine. Detroit's execution wasn't great early, and the Lions did put 31 points on the board. However, the offense seemed to lack rhythm for long stretches and finished just 5-of-13 on third down.

More concerning was the fact that Detroit's defense was about as stiff as a warm pat of margarine in the second half against the New Orleans Saints. The Lions escaped with a win, but they don't feel like title contenders and should feel very fortunate to be 1-0. -- Knox

The New England Patriots still haven't figured out the Seattle Seahawks, with bookend losses to end last season and open the current campaign.

Drake Maye's performance Wednesday is definitely concerning, because the quarterback had all offseason to figure out what went wrong during Super Bowl LX and fix those issues. Instead, he threw three interceptions during the season-opener, including when the Patriots were in game-tying field-goal position late in the contest, then admitted he grew impatient.

To make matters worse, star wide receiver AJ Brown, who was New England's prized offseason acquisition, suffered a high-ankle sprain during his Patriots debut. He's expected to miss six weeks, according to NFL Network's Ian Rapoport--which once again leaves New England without a legitimate playmaker at wide receiver. -- Sobleski

The Houston Texans' pass defense didn't have any answers for Josh Allen, who threw for 334 yards and two touchdowns. The Bills' dynamic signal-caller also ran for 23 yards and two scores.

The Texans defense has to take accountability for this season-opening loss, giving up 7.9 yards per play without a turnover. For comparison to the previous season, Houston allowed 4.8 yards per play and recorded a takeaway in all but two games, including the playoffs.

The Texans fall in our rankings, but they should be able to bounce back from an atypical leaky defensive performance. – Moton

During the summer, Chicago Bears head coach Ben Johnson told Dan Pompei of The Athletic that he wanted to field the highest-scoring offense in NFL history. Against the Carolina Panthers on Sunday, Chicago racked up 552 yards and 59 points.

The problem is that the Bears might have to have a historically good offense in order to repeat as NFC North champions. As was the case last season, the defense relied heavily on takeaways while giving up far too many yards (478, 7.7 per play) and points (37) for comfort. -- Knox

The Philadelphia Eagles don't lose openers under head coach Nick Sirianni—Sunday's victory over the Commanders makes the team 6-0 in Week 1 during his tenure. But Sirianni probably isn't doing cartwheels about how the Eagles won.

Jalen Hurts threw three touchdown passes but completed just 56 percent of his passes. The offense averaged six yards per play but converted less than half their third-down tries. The Philly pass rush was all but invisible, recording just one sack and two QB hits.

Now, some of that could just be rust—most of Philadelphia's starters spent the preseason in bubble wrap. A win is a win. And next week's trip to face the Tennessee Titans is hardly a daunting matchup.

But the Eagles have their sights set on SoFi Stadium and Super Bowl LXI, and if they are going to make a deep playoff run they need to tighten things up on both sides on the ball. -- Davenport

Week 1 Result: Lost vs. San Francisco 27-7

The Los Angeles Rams 2026 super team ate humble pie in Australia, but it would be an overreaction to say they'll be a disappointment this year.

Myles Garrett talked about getting over an offseason knee injury. He underwent arthroscopic knee surgery, according to The Ringer's Tom Pelissero . The Rams placed him on injured reserve, though he could return in a month or so. Aaron Donald didn't play.

If you're already selling your Rams stock, this analyst will buy it. Los Angeles was a Super Bowl contender before it acquired Garrett and Donald unretired; that doesn't change after a bad loss.

Even without Garrett, the Rams' defensive front should be much improved when Donald makes his on-field return. Los Angeles isn't going to give up 174 rushing yards to another opponent, and head coach Sean McVay will get last season's No. 1 offense going at home next Monday. -- Moton

The Jacksonville Jaguars weren't tested by the offensively inept Cleveland Browns, but it's still fair to acknowledge that Trevor Lawrence looked sharp, going 18-of-23 for 245 yards and four touchdowns. Keep in mind that he's completed fewer than 61 percent of his passes in back-to-back seasons. His accuracy is noteworthy, regardless of the opponent.

With all the talk about the Houston Texans defense, the Jaguars, after winning the AFC South title, are a bit overlooked among potential contenders this year. If Lawrence and Co. become more efficient on offense, this team will take another step in the right direction. Jacksonville may be a top-five team more so than a top-10 squad in the power rankings. -- Moton

Week 1 Result: Won at Indianapolis 41-23

Star power can be hard to beat. And Sunday in Indianapolis, Baltimore's offensive stars had themselves a game.

Quarterback Lamar Jackson threw for 324 yards and a score and ran for another touchdown. Running back Derrick Henry went off to the tune of 144 yards and three touchdowns. Wide receiver Zay Flowers caught five of six targets for 150 yards and a touchdown—in a half.

The defense got in on the act, too—veteran linebacker Roquan Smith piled up 11 tackles and picked off a pass. The final score of this game wasn't very close—but it's closer than the game itself was. The Ravens controlled this contest from the jump.

However, there could be a dark cloud amidst the sunlight. Both Flowers (hamstring) and rookie wideout Ja'Kobi Lane (wrist) left the game with injuries, and that could leave the Ravens thin at that position at home against the Saints in Week 2. – Davenport

Week 1 Result: Won vs. Los Angeles Rams 27-7

Head coach Kyle Shanahan should feel encouraged by what he saw out of his offense.

Quarterback Brock Purdy has a strong connection with free-agent acquisition Mike Evans. Deebo Samuel Sr. fit in like he never left. Both scored touchdowns. Rookie second-rounder Kaelon Black looks like a solid complement to Christian McCaffrey as the two split a majority of the carries.

If the 49ers' veteran-led offense and defense stay healthy, with the help of a few young players like Black, this team will be in the thick of an NFC West title race again. -- Moton

The Broncos claimed the AFC's No. 1 seed last season and may have reached the Super Bowl with a healthy Bo Nix at quarterback. Based on what we saw from the likes of Baltimore, Buffalo, and Jacksonville on Sunday, Denver's path back to the top seed won't be an easy one.

The Broncos will face their first test on Monday night against the rival Chiefs. -- Knox

The Buffalo Bills staked their claim as the NFL's best team with the most impressive victory from Week 1. Josh Allen and Co. went into Houston, faced the league's best defense and posted over 400 yards of total offense.

Obviously, Allen's presence alone gives the Bills an advantage over most, if not all of their opponents. The former league MVP contributed four touchdowns Sunday, including a pair of scores on the ground, which made the NFL's all-time leader among quarterbacks in career rushing touchdowns.

However, a reworked defense under new coordinator Jim Leonard deserves credit for coming up big late in the contest with two sacks and a forced fumble to end Houston's chances of taking a lead deep in the fourth quarter. -- Sobleski

The reigning Super Bowl champions found a way to get a victory against the New England Patriots without quarterback Sam Darnold, who suffered a hip injury on the first drive of the game.

Yes, backup Drew Lock steadied the Seahawks offense and avoided turnovers, but Seattle's fourth-quarter comeback is proof that this team isn't a flash-in-the-pan squad that will fade after its title run.

Led by play-calling head coach Mike Macdonald, Seattle fields one of the league's best defenses, and Jaxon Smith-Njigba continues to rise as a big-play star receiver.

The Seahawks should've been No. 1 to start our power rankings. They certainly belong there now. -- Moton

articles.title: New Cowboys Rumors Update Malik Hooker's Injury Status, Return Timeline After Exiting vs. Giants
articles.summary: Dallas Cowboys safety Malik Hooker could miss a month or more after suffering a fractured bone in his forearm in Sunday's 28-20 loss to the New York Giants, according to Ian Rapoport of NFL Network and ESPN.
articles.body:
Dallas Cowboys safety Malik Hooker could miss a month or more after suffering a fractured bone in his forearm in Sunday's 28-20 loss to the New York Giants, according to Ian Rapoport of NFL Network and ESPN.

Rapoport reported Hooker requires further testing to pin down a timeline for his recovery.

"While some breaks can mean a player is out six weeks, the hope is based on the specific bone and break, it's quicker than that," the NFL insider said.

Hooker was on the field for just 12 defensive snaps . After the game concluded, coach Brian Schottenheimer said the initial belief was that the veteran defensive back had fractured his forearm.

Hooker was the one of two defensive starters to go down in the defeat. Linebacker DeMarvion Overshown left with a hamstring injury.

On the basis of Sunday night, Dallas can ill afford to be shorthanded on defense. The team allowed 394 yards to the Giants, and that number doesn't portray how easily they moved the chains.

New York averaged 5.8 yards per play, went 9-of-11 on third downs, and possessed the ball for almost 37 minutes.

The Giants had seven offensive possessions. Four resulted in a touchdown and a fifth saw them run off the final 5:21 of the game to secure the victory.

Christian Parker's first game as defensive coordinator couldn't have gone much worse. For that reason alone, things are bound to improve in Week 2 against the Washington Commanders.

But it sounds like the Cowboys will be without Hooker, and an injured reserve designation could be in his future.

articles.title: NFL On Verge of Making History With High-Scoring Week 1 Ahead of Nix, Broncos vs. Mahomes, Chiefs
articles.summary: NFL offenses came out hot in the 2026 season, and might be about to record the highest Week 1 scoring average since the AFL and NFL merged in 1970.
articles.body:
NFL offenses came out hot in the 2026 season, and might be about to record the highest Week 1 scoring average since the AFL and NFL merged in 1970.

According to The Athletic's Jayna Bardahl , "Entering Monday's Week 1 capper between the Denver Broncos and Kansas City Chiefs, teams have scored 750 points, for an average of 50.0 points per game. According to the NFL, if that average holds, it would surpass the 49.4 points per game scored in Week 1 in 2012. That week featured a total of 791 points, so the Broncos and Chiefs need a combined 42 points to set the record."

Granted, the Broncos are expected to have one of the best defenses in football this season, so a low-scoring affair on Monday night—preventing the possible record—isn't out of the question.

As for the Week 1 offensive onslaught, Ben Johnson's Chicago Bears led the way, beating the Carolina Panthers 59-37. Chicago had a whopping 552 yards of total offense (and the Panthers weren't far behind with 478). Fireworks were not in short supply.

In total, 10 of the 30 teams who have played thus far scored 30 or more points, while half of the league's teams put up 25 or more points. Four games featured both teams in action scoring 25 or more points.

It was the type of week that fantasy football enthusiasts love, defensive purists hate and probably requires a whole lot of recovery sleep for NFL RedZone host Scott Hanson.

And barring a defensive showdown on Monday night, it also is about to set records.

articles.title: Herbert, Chargers Will 'Have Their Hands Full' vs. Cousins, Raiders After Cardinals Loss, Says Coach
articles.summary: After the Los Angeles Chargers opened the 2026 season with a surprising 26-14 loss to the Arizona Cardinals, some around the NFL are losing confidence in their chances of being successful going forward.
articles.body:
After the Los Angeles Chargers opened the 2026 season with a surprising 26-14 loss to the Arizona Cardinals, some around the NFL are losing confidence in their chances of being successful going forward.

The Athletic's Mike Sando spoke to an NFL coach who suggested that the Chargers could be in for another tough test in their Week 2 matchup against the Las Vegas Raiders.

"They are going to have their hands full with the Raiders next week, because the Raiders are organized, they have a veteran quarterback and their defensive front is decent," the coach said.

Sando noted that the Cardinals entered Week 1 as "the heaviest underdog (+10.5) by far." Still, they managed to limit Chargers star quarterback Justin Herbert to just 209 yards, a touchdown and an interception on 17-of-27 passing while sacking him three times.

The Raiders defeated the Miami Dolphins 27-13 on Sunday behind a three-touchdown performance from veteran quarterback Kirk Cousins. While Las Vegas is in the midst of a rebuild, it's clear that the team has enough talent to be competitive.

The Chargers will need to bounce back in Week 2, as they will face a tough slate after that with matchups against the Buffalo Bills, Seattle Seahawks, Denver Broncos, Kansas City Chiefs, Los Angeles Rams, Houston Texans and Baltimore Ravens, five of which are on the road. If they can't beat the Raiders, they won't have any chance against the NFL's elite squads.

articles.title: Patrick Mahomes’ kids deliver emotional message before his Chiefs return, revealing the special bond behind his ACL comeback
articles.summary: NFL News: Patrick Mahomes is set to return for the Kansas City Chiefs’ Week 1 game against the Denver Broncos after nine months of rehab for torn ACL and LCL in.
articles.body: Patrick Mahomes is set to return for the Kansas City Chiefs’ Week 1 game against the Denver Broncos after nine months of rehab for torn ACL and LCL in his left knee. But before the quarterback steps back onto the field, his children, Sterling and Bronze, gave him a message that brought the focus back to what mattered most during his recovery: being their dad.How did Patrick Mahomes’ kids support him during his ACL recovery?Mahomes has been open about how difficult the early part of his recovery was. The physical work was one challenge, but being unable to move around and play with his children was even harder for him.“Honestly, the toughest part was at the beginning, not being able to get up and chase my kids around,” Mahomes said. “I know it sounds crazy, but being a dad and being active, I always want to be around my kids and playing and stuff like that. That was tough. But once I was able to do that, it kinda motivated me to keep getting better and better.”In the voicemail shared by The Players’ Tribune, Sterling and Bronze said, “Hello Daddy. Daddy, I love you. I’m so happy that he gets to go back to playing football. I love you so much. Good job for all your rehab; we’re so happy that you get to play football again, and we get to watch you. You’re the best daddy in the world. I love you. I love you so much.”For Mahomes, those words came from the two people he was thinking about when the recovery felt hardest.Why did Patrick Mahomes’ return mean so much to Sterling and Bronze?Mahomes’ return is a moment for the Chiefs, but it is also a personal one for his children. Sterling, 5, and Bronze, 3, have grown up watching their father play football, so seeing him back on the field means they can once again watch him do what they know him for.Sterling has also shown an interest in sports herself. She plays soccer, while Bronze plays T-Ball.Mahomes suffered the ACL and LCL tears in his left knee during the Chiefs’ Week 15 loss to the Los Angeles Chargers in December 2025. He had surgery the next day and spent the offseason working toward his goal of being ready for Week 1. The Chiefs confirmed that he was a full participant in practice during the week leading into the opener, and the NFL reported that he had no injury designation for Monday’s game.The Chiefs had planned for Mahomes to return in Week 1, but his availability depended on how his knee responded. He stayed focused on reaching that target and did not play in the preseason as the team managed his comeback.Now, Mahomes is ready to return against Denver. His children’s message shows why this comeback is about more than football. Before his first game, they gave him a simple reminder of why all that work mattered.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Deshaun Watson will start in Week 2 for Browns vs. Bucs after Week 1 dud
articles.summary: Watson's status was unclear following a 34-10 loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars on Sunday in which Watson threw an interception on Cleveland's opening possess...
articles.body:
Deshaun Watson will start again in Week 2. Cleveland Browns head coach Todd Monken told reporters Monday that Watson will retain his job as starting quarterback for Sunday's game against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers .

Watson's status was unclear following a 34-10 loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars on Sunday in which he threw an interception on Cleveland's opening possession and the Browns didn't score a touchdown until the game was long decided with less than two minutes remaining.

"I anticipate that Deshaun will be our starter," Monken said when asked about Watson's status on Monday. "It's only been two weeks he's gotten all the reps. And there were some really good things on film. Some things that you can build on. …

"I did think that when he had time, when he understood the concepts, he didn't play tentative, that he let it rip. Even the touchdown at the end. Sure, that was garbage time."

Monken added that he believes that Watson has demonstrated reason to believe that he'll improve with time and more reps.

"There was a lot of things to build on," Monken continued. "Was it perfect? Of course not. Otherwise we wouldn't have scored as few points as we did. I'd like to see how we can build on that. I liked his week of practice last week. And I think he's only going to continue to get better."

Monken said he reached the decision to start Watson again after watching film from Sunday's game.

Watson got the start on Sunday after beating out second-year quarterback Shedeur Sanders for the job in the preseason. The start was Watson's first NFL game action since the 2024 season, when injuries and poor play further derailed his career.

Sanders started seven games in 2025 as a rookie and did nothing to demonstrate that he's a capable starting NFL quarterback while completing 56.6% of his passes and throwing seven touchdowns and 10 interceptions. The Browns didn't improve their quarterback room in the offseason, and Monken was left to decide between Sanders and Watson as his starting quarterback.

Cleveland's offense was largely inept on Sunday as Jacksonville opened a 31-0 lead in the third quarter. The Browns drove inside Jacksonville's 30-yard line on their opening possession, but Watson threw an interception on his third pass of the game.

Watson later fumbled a ball that the Browns recovered and struggled at times to identify open receivers downfield . Cleveland's only touchdown arrived with 1:56 remaining in a 24-point game when Watson found Denzel Boston with a 46-yard pass into the end zone that salvaged his final stat line.

Watson finished the day completing 16-of-22 passes for 205 yards with 1 touchdown, 1 interception and 1 fumble. He took five sacks.

Will Watson still be Cleveland's starter in first home game?

After the game, Monken was non-committal about Watson's status for Week 2, which, like Sunday, will take place on the road. Cleveland won't have its first home game until Week 3 against the Carolina Panthers .

Browns fans aren't happy with Watson, who's been a bust on the field since the Browns traded for him in 2022 despite a scandal in which he was accused of sexual misconduct by 27 women . They booed him during his only home appearance in the preseason, and Watson responded by chastising them while speaking with media.

A three-time Pro Bowler with the Houston Texans , Watson has struggled with poor play and injuries during his entire Browns stint. His time as Cleveland's starter appeared to be done in 2024, but when Cleveland failed to upgrade its quarterback room, he got the job again for at least the first two weeks of this season.

articles.title: Deshaun Watson's Status as QB1 Over Shedeur Sanders Addressed By Browns HC After Blowout Loss
articles.summary: For right now, Cleveland Browns coach Todd Monken isn't expecting to make a quarterback change ahead of the team's Week 2 game against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.
articles.body:
For right now, Cleveland Browns coach Todd Monken isn't expecting to make a quarterback change ahead of the team's Week 2 game against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.

Monken told reporters Monday he "anticipates" sticking with Deshaun Watson under center.

Watson threw an interception on Cleveland's first drive Sunday, and that set the tone in a 34-10 loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars. He finished with 205 passing yards and one touchdown along with two turnovers. He was also sacked five times.

With the Browns in the midst of a rebuild, one argument in favor of picking Watson over Shedeur Sanders or Dillon Gabriel is that he has a clear edge in experience. Maybe he can be a steady hand for one year while the franchise assesses its long-term options and lays a foundation.

But Watson doesn't even look like a good stopgap option anymore. The offense was out of sorts until the Jaguars built a big enough lead to where they could coast to the finish line.

At some point, it becomes impossible to ignore the fact Watson was last a viable starter in 2020, and he has missed two full seasons since then.

In addition, whatever goodwill the three-time Pro Bowler had left in Cleveland evaporated with his combative press conference following the Browns' preseason loss to the Buffalo Bills in August.

Still, The MMQB's Albert Breer reported Watson was "widely seen internally as the best option," hence his QB1 status.

If the 31-year-old fails to make major improvements, it's going to be difficult to say he's keeping the starting job on merit rather than the Browns' desire to recoup anything from what is one of the worst contracts in NFL history.

And the longer Sanders is holding a clipboard, the more it will appear to be a vote of no confidence from his coaches.

articles.title: El auge de la cerveza sin alcohol en EE.UU. une a dos estrellas de la NFL
articles.standfirst: Drake Maye y Dak Prescott se unen a la empresa especializada en esta bebida Athletic Brewing Company como deportistas-propietarios
articles.summary: Drake Maye y Dak Prescott se unen a la empresa especializada en esta bebida Athletic Brewing Company como deportistas-propietarios
articles.body: Athletic Brewing Company, la cervecera estadounidense dedicada exclusivamente a bebidas sin alcohol, anunció hace unos días una asociación de varios año con dos de los quarterbacks estrella de la NFL, Drake Maye y Dak Prescott. Dicha asociación va un poco más allá, pues ambos han entrado como lo que denominan ‘deportistas-propietarios’ y participarán en campañas de marketing exclusivas para la marca. Athletic es una marca cada vez más consolidada y está tirando del deporte para conseguir llegar al público. Mantiene importantes alianzas en el mundo del fútbol americano profesional, fútbol, béisbol, lacrosse, hockey, deporte universitarios… La marca está ya en muchos recintos deportivos. No cabe duda de que tanto Prescott como Maye están apostando fuerte por el auge de la cerveza sin alcohol en todo Estados Unidos. En 2026, el mercado mundial de esta bebida se ha valorado entre 26.200 y 28.620 millones de dólares. De hecho, un estudio publicado hace 12 meses por Gallup (empresa estadounidense de análisis, consultoría de gestión y encuestas de opinión pública), concluyó que el porcentaje de adultos estadounidenses que afirman consumir alcohol ha descendido al 54%. Se trata del porcentaje más bajo en casi 90 años, y es que Gallup ha realizado un seguimiento de los hábitos de consumo de alcohol de los estadounidenses desde 1939 y conoce perfectamente las tendencias del mercado. Según indican en su estudio, la caída del consumo de alcohol en los últimos años es notable. "La historia de crecimiento de Athletic y su mentalidad de superación me llamaron la atención de inmediato", dijo Maye en el comunicado que anunciaba su asociación con la cervecera fundada por Bill Shufelt y John Walker. Prescott, por su parte, indicó: "A medida que me he involucrado más en el mundo de los negocios, me he vuelto cada vez más selectivo con las oportunidades que busco y las personas con las que elijo trabajar".

articles.title: Vikings' Kyler Murray in concussion protocol after leaving Week 1, but able to take part in team meetings
articles.summary: Kyler Murray showed some decent progress Monday after leaving Sunday's game with a concussion.
articles.body:
The Minnesota Vikings lost Kyler Murray early in Week 1, but it didn't matter. Backup Carson Wentz tossed three touchdowns to help the Vikings stun the Green Bay Packers with a 22-point fourth quarter to earn the victory .

But that wasn't how things were supposed to go. After signing with the team in the offseason, Murray was expected to start for the Vikings and — hypothetically — show growth under Kevin O'Connell.

That might be on hold for a little bit, as Murray was placed in the concussion protocol after Week 1, O'Connell confirmed Monday.

Despite that, however, it sounds like Murray is doing much better than anticipated, and was able to take part in team meetings.

Because of that, Murray is considered day-to-day ahead of Week 2.

That's a promising development for both Murray and the Vikings. Following the team's Week 1 win, Minnesota's job could get even more difficult in Week 2, when the Chicago Bears come to town. The Bears are fresh off a 59-point performance in a win over the Carolina Panthers.

While Wentz should be commended for his performance on short notice, the Vikings' offense might have an easier time keeping pace with the Bears if Murray's dual-threat ability is under center in Week 2. It sounds like that scenario is in play based on Murray's progress Monday.

Ultimately, though, whether Murray plays in Week 2 will be determined by both the Vikings' team doctors and an independent neurological consultant. Things seem to be in a good spot Monday, but Murray will need to show further improvement during the week in order to be cleared.

articles.title: Bears Announce Malik Muhammad Personal News After Win Over Panthers
articles.summary: The Bears announced personal news involving Malik Muhammad after Chicago’s Week 1 win over the Carolina Panthers. The post Bears Announce Malik Muhammad Pers...
articles.body:
The Chicago Bears got their 2026 NFL season off to a spectacular start on Sunday, putting up a record 59 points — breaking a franchise record for points in a season opener that had stood since 1948 — while allowing 37 in a wild win over the Carolina Panthers .

Quarterback Caleb Williams ran for two touchdowns and threw for two more, while D'Andre Swift carried for three TDs in the Week 1 victory.

The morning after the game, the Bears announced some personal news about their rookie cornerback who came away with his first NFL interception on Sunday.

Malik Muhammad II celebrated a birthday Monday. The Bears ' fourth-round draft pick this year turns 22 years old.

The Bears wished their rookie a happy birthday on their social media channels, one day after Muhammad recorded that interception to go with three tackles in the highest-scoring season opener the NFL has ever seen.

Malik Muhammad II Shines in Historic NFL Debut

The combined 96 points at Bank of America Stadium broke the previous record for a season opener by eight, set in 2018 when Tampa Bay outlasted New Orleans 48-40, according to an Associated Press report . Quarterback Caleb Williams threw for 269 yards and two touchdowns while running for 65 yards and two more scores, and running back D'Andre Swift piled up 124 yards and three touchdowns on the ground.

Muhammad stepped into the starting lineup at nickel cornerback after safety Xavier Woods was ruled out before kickoff, according to A to Z Sports . The rookie promptly became Carolina's preferred target, seeing a team-high nine looks among Chicago defensive backs while allowing five catches for 67 yards, a completion rate of 55.6 percent and a passer rating against of just 39.8, as tallied by Sports Illustrated .

The signature moment came on a diving interception in the closing seconds of the first half, and Muhammad also broke up a fourth-down throw intended for Tetairoa McMillan to end another Panthers possession.

Muhammad stayed grounded afterward, pointing to the defense's larger struggles rather than his own big night.

"We definitely have a lot to clean up, and I know that wasn't good enough, especially on the defensive side. I know our coaches feel the same way too," as quoted by A to Z Sports .

Muhammad was born Sept. 14, 2004, in Dallas and grew up in the Oak Cliff area, introduced to the sport by his uncles when he was barely out of diapers, according to ChicagoBears.com . He is the third-oldest of eight siblings and the oldest boy in the family.

At South Oak Cliff High School, Muhammad closed his prep career with an interception returned for a touchdown in a state title game, adding 60 tackles and 14 pass breakups as a senior, according to a scouting report from NFL Draft Buzz .

He carried that production into a three-year run at Texas, appearing in 41 games with 29 starts and finishing with 97 tackles, three interceptions and 16 pass breakups, numbers the official ChicagoBears.com team site noted when Chicago traded up in the fourth round of this year's draft to select him.

The Bears sent picks No. 129 and No. 144 to Carolina for picks No. 124 and No. 166, landing Muhammad at 124th overall before signing him to a four-year rookie deal worth roughly $5.48 million.

That trade partner makes Sunday's outcome land a little differently. The cornerback Chicago acquired by dealing with the Panthers spent his NFL debut making life miserable for Carolina's passing game, then turned 22 the next day with a signature win already on his resume.

articles.title: What We Learned From Bryce Lance’s Saints Debut
articles.summary: Bryce Lance won’t ever forget his NFL debut, for reasons both good and bad. Of course, just the chance to suit up for the New Orleans Saints and be on the fi...
articles.body:
Bryce Lance won't ever forget his NFL debut, for reasons both good and bad.

Of course, just the chance to suit up for the New Orleans Saints and be on the field in a regular season NFL game has to be a special memory that will last a long time.

But on the flip side, it was Lance who watched the game-deciding 2-point conversion pass from Tyler Shough fly over his head and out of the end zone. There was nothing Lance could've done — the ball was thrown too far and too high — but he was the closest to it. It was he who had the up-close view to a heartbreaking Saints loss.

In football parlance, though, it's already on to next week. The Saints have more games to play. Lance has more positive impressions to make.

He already did plenty to impress in Week 1, though, and it's worth taking a deeper look at it.

Lance ended up putting together a very solid stat line of three catches for 42 yards in his NFL debut.

He played the third-most snaps among Saints receivers behind Chris Olave and Devaughn Vele , who both had big games.

Lance was targeted four times by Shough and brought in three of those, including a long gain of 19 yards.

As a fourth-round pick out of North Dakota State, Lance wasn't viewed as an entirely sure thing. Some folks liked him more than others in the draft process, but at 6-foot-3 with solid athleticism, Lance certainly looks the part.

He probably didn't get positive vibes in the pre-draft analysis world from the fact that his brother Trey was a draft bust for the 49ers , either.

That's not Bryce's burden to bear, though, and he looked comfortable on the NFL stage on Sunday.

Lance's longest game came on his first career catch, which came in a highly encouraging moment for the rookie.

The Saints were in the two-minute drill just before halftime, which is a situation that young players have to get comfortable in.

Lance burst off the line and appeared to correctly recognize that the Lions were in a zone defense, so he settled right into an opening between four spread out defenders each in their own zone.

Shough clearly saw the same opening Lance did, and they were on the same page to complete the connection:

That's just a lot of positive instincts for Lance in a singular moment in his NFL debut.

Lance also had a crucial 15-yard catch on fourth-and-12 as the Saints put together the game-tying drive in the fourth quarter, and it required some seriously strong hands through contact:

With Olave and Vele around, and the eventual return of first-rounder Jordyn Tyson from injury, Lance won't always be a huge contributor.

But he's already shown that when called upon, he can deliver. That's quite the message to send in an NFL debut.

Cam Skattebo celebrated his first touchdown of the season with his signature backflip in the Giants' Week 1 win over the Cowboys

The touchdown marked Skattebo's return after a season-ending ankle injury last October

Fans were unsure if he would perform the flip after a mishap during a summer Fanatics Fest appearance

Cam Skattebo is back like he never left!

The New York Giants running back, 24, performed his signature backflip in the end zone to celebrate his first touchdown of the season in Big Blue's home opener against the Dallas Cowboys at MetLife Stadium on Sunday, Sept. 13.

Skattebo scored a three-yard rushing touchdown in the first quarter to give the Giants an early 7-0 lead in their eventual 28-20 victory over the Cowboys. In classic Skatt fashion, he launched himself into a roundoff flip followed by a backflip to commemorate putting points on the board.

The touchdown was especially significant for the second-year running back, whose rookie season was cut short last October when he suffered a brutal, season-ending ankle injury .

It was an electric scene at MetLife Stadium on Sunday night, as quarterback Jaxson Dart tossed three touchdowns to give new coach John Harbaugh a win in his debut.

Entering Sunday's game, it was unclear if Skattebo would perform his signature celebration following a mishap at Michael Rubin's multi-day Fanatics Fest in New York City over the summer.

At the time, Skattebo stepped onto the Fanatics Fest stage, lifted his pant leg to show off the massive scar on his right leg and then launched into a backflip in front of the crowd. However, his landing wasn't stable and he awkwardly fell to the ground.

The running back later ensured fans he would "not hurt" himself before the season began.

Skattebo cited the "bouncy" floor — a WWE runway that Fanatics set up for athletes to get a wrestling-style entrance — as the reason for his stumble.

A fourth-round pick by the Giants in 2025, Skattebo tallied 410 yards and five touchdowns before last season's injury.

articles.title: Jaguars announce injury update on Brian Thomas Jr. & his Week 2 status
articles.summary: The Jaguars 3rd year star WR left the game on Sunday with a shoulder injury.
articles.body:
The Jacksonville Jaguars received a scare involving one of their most important offensive players during Sunday's NFL Week 1 win over the Cleveland Browns . Brian Thomas Jr. left the game in the second quarter with a shoulder injury and initially was listed as questionable to return, creating immediate concern for a Jacksonville offense that had already jumped out to a big lead.

Fortunately, the latest update is much more encouraging than it initially appeared, and the Jaguars came away with a 34-10 victory over Cleveland.

Jacksonville Jaguars wide receiver Brian Thomas Jr. (7) catches a pass during the first day of NFL Training Camp at the Miller Electric Center on Wednesday, July 29, 2026, in Jacksonville, Fla.

Thomas headed to the locker room with Jacksonville's medical staff after apparently injuring his shoulder. The Jaguars announced that he was questionable to return, and he had already made an impact before leaving, catching all three of his targets for 40 yards.

The good news came later in the second quarter when Thomas returned to the field. He was able to participate in the Jaguars' final drive of the first half, providing an important indication that the injury wasn't severe enough to keep him sidelined.

Thomas ultimately finished the afternoon with three catches for 40 yards, although he wasn't involved in any of Trevor Lawrence 's four touchdown passes.

The Jaguars will still be watching his shoulder

While Thomas' return is certainly encouraging, the shoulder remains something to monitor heading into Week 2.

The injury is particularly noteworthy because Thomas dealt with a shoulder issue during training camp. He suffered that earlier scare during a joint practice with Tampa Bay but recovered in time to become a full participant before the season opener.

Jacksonville certainly has plenty of weapons, with Parker Washington , Travis Hunter and Jakobi Meyers all capable of contributing. But Thomas remains one of the most important pieces of the offense and entered 2026 looking to bounce back from a disappointing second NFL season.

He also reached an impressive milestone Sunday, surpassing 2,000 career receiving yards and becoming the second-youngest player in Jaguars history to reach that mark.

For now, the biggest takeaway is simple: Thomas avoided what initially looked like a potentially serious injury and returned to finish the game. That should provide Jaguars fans and fantasy managers with plenty of optimism heading into Week 2.

articles.title: Rookie QBs rarely beat Bill Belichick, but Clemson's Tait Reynolds will get chance
articles.summary: UNC opens ACC play at Clemson, where freshman QB Tait Reynolds will try to do something that hasn't been accomplished a lot vs. Bill Belichick.
articles.body:
CHAPEL HILL — UNC football coach Bill Belichick smiled when asked what a defense can do to make a young quarterback look and feel like a freshman.

"Play good," Belichick said with a smirk.

During his 24 seasons with the NFL's New England Patriots , Belichick's defenses built a reputation for frustrating inexperienced QBs. His teams lost to only seven rookie starting signal-callers during his time in Massachusetts.

New York Giants QB Tommy Devito became No. 7 in 2023.

In his debut season at UNC, the Tar Heels had a 1-1 record against freshmen QBs. UNC lost to Cal's Jaron Keawe-Sagapolutele before beating Syracuse's Joe Filardi, a walk-on and lacrosse player.

Next up is Clemson freshman Tait Reynolds, who will try to join that list of young QBs to take down Belichick. The Tar Heels (2-0) open ACC play against the Tigers (1-1) on Sept. 19 (Noon ET, ESPN) in Death Valley.

"Tait is a guy we spent some time on last year in the recruiting process," Belichick said.

"Really athletic kid, very, very productive in some of the high school tape that we saw. I'm sure he's gonna be a really good quarterback in the ACC and college football. He's very athletic, hard guy to tackle, has a good arm, can make all the throws."

Reynolds, a 6-foot-2, 215-pound freshman from Arizona, has completed 20 of 33 passes for 200 yards through two games. He also has 19 carries for 29 yards. Last season, Keawe-Sagapolutele completed 21 of 39 passes for 209 yards and a touchdown, with UNC logging two sacks. Filardi was 4 of 18 for 39 yards.

UNC's defense has been stingy through two games this year. The Tar Heels have allowed 13 points, holding TCU and ETSU scoreless during a 105-minute stretch. Opposing quarterbacks are averaging 176.5 yards with no touchdowns, one interception and seven sacks allowed vs. the Tar Heels.

Whether it was Reynolds or senior Christopher Vizzina , who's dealing with an injury, Belichick doesn't expect significant shifts from the Tigers' offense.

"I think, in a way, they're both similar. They both can run the ball and they have quarterback runs incorporated in their offense," Belichick said.

". … Whoever they feel most confident with – I guess Tait in this case – that's what we're gonna have to get ready for. But I don't think the offense is going to change dramatically with either player. I'd say their skills are within a range of similarity."

For Belichick, it goes far beyond the quarterback when trying to slow down Clemson . Throughout his 20-minute press conference, Belichick highlighted the talent of wide receivers TJ Moore and Bryant Wesco Jr..

"It's hard with Clemson. Kind of similar to TCU, they attack across the field on every play," Belichick said.

"The ball could get handed off, the quarterback could keep it, or if he sees an advantage outside, he can just raise up and throw the ball to the perimeter. You have to defend from sideline to sideline. … It's more than just the quarterback."

Ultimately, Belichick said the key remains the same regardless of who lines up behind center.

"It really comes down to team defense," he said. "Everybody doing their jobs."

articles.title: Cowboys S Malik Hooker reportedly has fractured forearm, expected to miss multiple weeks
articles.summary: A Dallas Cowboys defense that struggled in a disappointing Week 1 loss to the New York Giants got more bad news Monday.
articles.body:
Per NFL Network's Ian Rapoport , starting safety Malik Hooker sustained a fractured forearm in Sunday's game and is expected to miss multiple weeks. The report confirmed head coach Brian Schottenheimer's postgame concern that Hooker had sustained a broken bone.

Per the report, Hooker will consult with a hand specialist for a more precise prognosis.

The Cowboys also lost starting linebacker Demarian Overshown to a hamstring injury during Sunday's game. As of Monday afternoon, his status moving forward was unclear.

Hooker is a 10-season NFL veteran and Dallas' starting free safety. He's played for the Cowboys since 2021 and has been a full-time starter since 2023.

Cowboys' secondary couldn't contain Jaxson Dart , Giants

The loss of Hooker is a blow to a secondary that struggled to contain New York's passing game in Sunday's 28-20 loss. Giants quarterback Jaxson Dart completed 23 of 29 passes for 230 yards with 3 touchdowns and no turnovers. Giants receivers repeatedly ran free through busted downfield coverages.

The loss marks another disapointing start to a Cowboys season that started with hope . Dallas will now face immediate pressure to win in Week 2 in another NFC East matchup against the Washington Commanders .

From there, the Cowboys face a difficult five-game stretch with games against the Ravens , Texans , Buccaneers , Packers and Eagles in consecutive weeks. If they don't figure out some adjustments on both sides of the ball, their season could spiral quickly.

articles.title: Macklemore says he was kicked off of Ed Sheeran's tour after Robert Kraft intervened with 'ultimatum'
articles.summary: In a statement, Kraft defended the decision to bar Macklemore, who expressed vocal support for Palestine at Sheeran's concert earlier this month, from playin...
articles.body:
Amid the news that Macklemore has been dropped as an opener from Ed Sheeran's North American tour, the rapper has alleged that New England Patriots owner Robert Kraft intervened to get him removed.

In a lengthy statement posted on Instagram, Macklemore alleged that Kraft had called Sheeran ahead of the singer's concert at Gillette Stadium, which is owned by Kraft. In what Macklemore called a "f***ed up position" for Sheeran, Kraft allegedly barred Macklemore from performing in the stadium and had "rallied" other stadium owners to issue an "ultimatum."

"Last Monday, in the middle of all the media attention surrounding Pink and what I said at MetLife, Ed told me that Robert Kraft called him," Macklemore wrote. "Ed told me that Kraft said I would not be allowed to perform in his stadium. Ed also told me that Kraft had rallied some of the other stadium owners and collectively they gave him an ultimatum: if Macklemore stays on the tour, you will not be allowed to play in our venues."

Macklemore opened for Sheeran on Sept. 4 and 5 at New Jersey's MetLife Stadium. During his performance, Macklemore called for a "Free Palestine" in a speech before performing his song "Hind's Hall," which was written in support of pro-Palestine protests. The performance drew criticism from many, including singer P!nk , and received a significant amount of media attention.

Macklemore, whose real name is Benjamin Haggerty, has been vocal about his support for Palestine in recent years, something that he said challenged Sheeran's "typical apolitical stance."

Sheeran's tour continues on Saturday at Philadelphia 's Lincoln Financial Field. He is set to perform two nights at Gillette Stadium after that, on Sept. 25 and 26.

In response, Kraft issued a statement defending the decision to bar Macklemore from playing at Gillette, saying that he has focused on fighting antisemitism and feels "a responsibility to stand up when I believe that line has been crossed."

"Gillette Stadium has a longstanding commitment to providing a welcoming environment for all guests and ensuring that events held at our venue do not provide a platform for hate speech," Kraft wrote, via The Athletic's Jonathan Jones . "Based on Macklemore's recent actions, material shared from the stage during Ed Sheeran's shows in New Jersey, and a broader history of antisemitic rhetoric and imagery that we believe has been deeply offensive and hurtful to the Jewish community, we determined that his participation in the September 25th and 26th concerts at Gillette Stadium would cross that line. "This decision is not about diminishing the suffering of innocent Palestinians or denying anyone the right to advocate on their behalf. Their pain and loss are real."

"Gillette Stadium has a longstanding commitment to providing a welcoming environment for all guests and ensuring that events held at our venue do not provide a platform for hate speech," Kraft wrote, via The Athletic's Jonathan Jones . "Based on Macklemore's recent actions, material shared from the stage during Ed Sheeran's shows in New Jersey, and a broader history of antisemitic rhetoric and imagery that we believe has been deeply offensive and hurtful to the Jewish community, we determined that his participation in the September 25th and 26th concerts at Gillette Stadium would cross that line.

"This decision is not about diminishing the suffering of innocent Palestinians or denying anyone the right to advocate on their behalf. Their pain and loss are real."

Kraft did not address Macklemore's claim that the Patriots owner rallied other stadium owners to pressure Sheeran into dropping the rapper as an opener.

In his statement, Macklemore did not mention which of the other stadium owners were involved in the ultimatum, but most of the remaining stops on Sheeran's United States leg of the tour are NFL stadiums. Some of these stadiums, like Lincoln Financial Field, AT&T Stadium in Arlington and Atlanta 's Mercedes-Benz, are technically owned by the city or state, but are operated by the NFL ownership. Only Charlotte's Bank of America Stadium is owned outright by Carolina Panthers owner David Tepper, similar to Gillette Stadium and Kraft.
