articles.title: Vikings HC Reacts to 'Violent, Physical Play' That Caused Kyler Murray Injury vs. Packers
articles.summary: The Minnesota Vikings lost their starting quarterback early in Sunday's game against the Green Bay Packers after Kyler Murray suffered a concussion caused by a big hit as he was sliding.
articles.body:
The Minnesota Vikings lost their starting quarterback early in Sunday's game against the Green Bay Packers after Kyler Murray suffered a concussion caused by a big hit as he was sliding.

Speaking to reporters Monday, Vikings head coach Kevin O'Connell called it a "violent, physical play," but added that he doesn't "put any fault on anybody there."

In the first quarter of Murray's first game with the Vikings, he was scrambling and attempted to slide, but took a hit from Packers safety Javon Bullard, who was flagged for unnecessary roughness on the play.

Murray was evaluated for a concussion and later ruled out for the rest of the game. He finished with just 18 passing yards and an interception, completing three of his five passes.

While O'Connell said he didn't place blame on anyone for the play, Vikings right tackle Brian O'Neill, who shoved Bullard afterwards, regretted not standing up for his quarterback more.

"It was so bang, bang," O'Neill told reporters . "You don't want to freak out if you're wrong. I was probably wrong to not freak out more than that. So I kind of wish I took a shot at him."

Murray was listed as day-by-day on Monday, and O'Connell said he was able to participate in team meetings, which is a good sign that he'll at least have a chance to play in Week 2.

After Murray came out of the game, he was replaced by veteran Carson Wentz, who threw for 133 yards and three touchdowns, helping Minnesota score 29 unanswered points to win 39-22.

The Vikings would prefer to get Murray back on the field by Sunday, but Wentz's performance against the Packers showed he can at least hold his own against the Chicago Bears.

articles.title: Ladd McConkey Injury Update Provided by Chargers' Jim Harbaugh, Latest on WR After Exiting vs. Cards
articles.summary: After a Week 1 upset against the Arizona Cardinals, the Los Angeles Chargers could be without their star wide receiver in Week 2.
articles.body:
After a Week 1 upset against the Arizona Cardinals, the Los Angeles Chargers could be without their star wide receiver in Week 2.

Head coach Jim Harbaugh told reporters Monday that Ladd McConkey is dealing with a rib injury and is day-to-day heading into a matchup against the Las Vegas Raiders on Sunday.

During the third quarter of Sunday's loss to the Cardinals, McConkey was attempting to catch a pass from Justin Hebrert across the middle of the field when a hard hit sent him to the ground.

The wide receiver was clearly shaken up on the play and was holding his chest before exiting.

Before the injury, McConkey was putting together a solid game with 82 yards and a touchdown on five receptions. With McConkey sidelined for the final quarter, the Chargers dropped their season opener 26-14 in one of the more surprising results of Week 1.

Herbert struggled in the loss as he threw for 209 yards, a touchdown and an interception.

McConkey, who is in his third NFL season, was a standout for the Chargers as a rookie as he recorded 1,149 receiving yards and seven touchdowns. He took a step back amid struggles for the Chargers' offense last year, collecting 789 yards and six touchdowns.

After his Week 1 performance, McConkey appears on the way for a bounceback year, but he'll first have to avoid missing time following the injury on Sunday.

Los Angeles came into the season as a potential Super Bowl contender, but a rough showing in Week 1 quickly tempered expectations for the team. The Chargers have what should be a manageable game against the Las Vegas Raiders on Sunday, but the matchup against the Cardinals was also seen as an easy win.

If McConkey is forced to miss Week 2, it will only make things more difficult.

articles.title: Chargers HC Jim Harbaugh after Week 1 loss: 'I wish we played our starters more in the preseason'
articles.summary: Los Angeles is coming off a surprising 26-14 loss to Arizona.
articles.body:
Los Angeles Chargers head coach Jim Harbaugh told reporters on Monday following the team's Week 1 loss to the Arizona Cardinals that he regretted his choice to rest starters for much of the preseason . Harbaugh pointed out that he believed the team made several "preseason-type mistakes" that could have been avoided with more game reps for the starters ahead of the regular season.

The Chargers were expected to be a playoff contender this season. This was due to the hiring of offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel, with many excited to see how creative he could be with quarterback Justin Herbert , who has not been able to lead the team to a playoff win in multiple appearances.

McDaniel and Herbert got plenty of work in during offseason practices. The first game of the regular season, though, did not go their way.

Herbert finished the game 17-of-27 passing for 209 yards with a touchdown and an interception. He also scrambled five times, picking up 29 yards.

The offense looked fine at the start, scoring a rushing touchdown on its first drive of the game. LA's next three possessions ended in a fumble, a turnover on downs and a third-quarter punt.

Herbert finally found the end zone later in the third quarter, connecting with wide receiver Ladd McConkey for an 8-yard score.

After the score, though, the offensive output stopped. The Chargers ended the game with a punt, a blocked punt, an interception and then back-to-back turnovers on downs.

The interception was especially problematic. Herbert looked like he threw a prayer, hoping for the best, but it was easily intercepted in double coverage.

Harbaugh's comments were not only tied to the offense. LA's defense allowed 26 points to Jacoby Brissett and the No. 3 overall pick Jeremiyah Love in Mike LaFleur's head-coaching debut.

The Chargers had seven penalties for 64 yards, while the Cardinals had eight for 111 yards. LA, though, had two turnovers compared to none for Arizona and went 2 for 8 on third downs and 0-3 on fourth-down attempts.

The Week 1 home loss stings, but the Chargers will have to shake it off quickly. Los Angeles will return to SoFi Stadium in Week 2 and welcome the Las Vegas Raiders .

While that may seem like an easier matchup on paper, the Raiders are coming into the game after a 27-13 Week 1 win over the Miami Dolphins , and may have tight end Brock Bowers back, who missed the opener after a procedure on his knee.

articles.title: Jim Harbaugh Regrets Not Playing Starters More in NFL Preseason After Week 1 Loss to Cardinals
articles.summary: The Los Angeles Chargers started the season with a disappointing 26-14 loss against the Arizona Cardinals, and largely resting the starters during the preseason may have played a factor.
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Chargers started the season with a disappointing 26-14 loss against the Arizona Cardinals, and largely resting the starters during the preseason may have played a factor.

"We made some preseason type of mistakes," head coach Jim Harbaugh told reporters Monday. "Now I wish we played our starters more in the preseason to give them some game reps."

NFL teams have largely moved toward keeping their starters sidelined for much of the preseason due to the 17-game regular season and the desire to keep key players healthy. But the result in recent years has been some sloppy starts to the regular season, especially for teams adjusting to new head coaches or offensive coordinators.

The Chargers fall into the latter camp, bringing in former Miami Dolphins head coach Mike McDaniel as offensive coordinator. After managing 268 yards of total offense, 22:29 in time of possession, two turnovers and three sacks taken, it certainly looked like the offense could have used more time to gel in the new system.

articles.title: Isiah Pacheco Injury Update, Latest Rumors on Lions RB's Timeline to Return After Surgery Decision
articles.summary: The Detroit Lions will be relying on starting running back Jahmyr Gibbs more than ever in the 2026 season.
articles.body:
The Detroit Lions will be relying on starting running back Jahmyr Gibbs more than ever in the 2026 season.

According to Ian Rapoport of NFL Network, backup running back Isiah Pacheco may be out until at least December after undergoing back surgery.

The Lions had previously announced that Pacheco had been placed on injured reserve, ruling him out for at least the first four games of the season. Head coach Dan Campbell announced on Monday that Pacheco is expected to miss a "significant amount of time" after surgery.

With Pacheco sidelined, Detroit pulled out a 31-30 overtime victory over the New Orleans Saints in Week 1. Gibbs ran for 156 yards and two touchdowns on 29 carries. Sione Vaki (two carries for seven yards) and Jared Goff (two carries for two yards) were the only other players to have carries for the Lions.

Pacheco signed a one-year deal with Detroit in March after spending the first four years of his career with the Kansas City Chiefs, with whom he won two Super Bowls. His signing came after the Lions traded veteran running back David Montgomery to the Houston Texans, breaking up the "Sonic and Knuckles" tandem between him and Gibbs.

A seventh-round pick in the 2022 NFL draft, Pacheco showed promise early in his career with over 1,700 rushing yards across his first two seasons. He suffered a fractured fibula early in the 2024 season and hasn't been the same since, finishing the 2025 campaign with 118 carries for 462 yards and one touchdown.

Still, the Lions were hoping that a healthy Pacheco would be able to take the load off of Gibbs, who is already one of the top workhorse running backs in the league. Gibbs signed a three-year contract extension worth up to $75.5 million last month, making him the highest-paid running back in NFL history.

Without Pacheco available, the Lions will have Vaki and Jacob Saylors spell Gibbs from time to time, but it's safe to say that the three-time Pro Bowler will be getting the lion's share of the carries to start the season.

articles.title: Myles Garrett: Los Angeles Rams star needs knee operation
articles.summary: The Los Angeles Rams' defensive end Myles Garrett needs a knee operation which will sideline him for at least four weeks.
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Rams' defensive end Myles Garrett needs a knee operation which will sideline him for at least four weeks.

The reigning defensive player of the year joined the Rams from the Cleveland Browns in the summer in one of the biggest trades in NFL history.

The 30-year-old made his Rams debut in their season-opening game against the San Francisco 49ers last week as the Super Bowl favourites suffered a 27-7 defeat in Australia.

The two-time defensive player of the year missed most of training camp with a knee problem but after the game it became clear he would need minor surgery.

The Rams have placed Garrett on their injured reserve (IR) list, which means he must miss at least four games.

"I don't really [have a timeline] yet," said Rams head coach Sean McVay.

"It's all contingent upon [surgery]. You feel good about it. But I think it'd be unfair to him, without having the totality of all the information, to put any sort of timeline on it.

"We know that he'll be available in four weeks potentially, so we'll just take that a day at a time."

The Rams' defence has also been boosted by three-time defensive player of the year Aaron Donald coming out of retirement.

But the 35-year-old did not travel to Australia and coach McVay said the Rams are yet to decide if he will play next week against the New York Giants.

Garrett broke the NFL single-season record with 23 sacks last season but against the 49ers he failed to register a tackle for just the fourth time in his career.

Following the game, Garrett said: "I've got to find a way to recover and get back to the player I know I can be and I've shown that I've been before."

articles.title: Joey Porter Jr. Status Updated by Steelers' Mike McCarthy amid New NFL Trade Rumors
articles.summary: Amid trade rumors surrounding Joey Porter Jr., Pittsburgh Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy gave an update on the cornerback's status after he missed Sunday's season opener.
articles.body:
Amid trade rumors surrounding Joey Porter Jr., Pittsburgh Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy gave an update on the cornerback's status after he missed Sunday's season opener.

"We'll have a good plan for him on Wednesday. Hopefully he'll do more," McCarthy told reporters about Porter.

ESPN's Adam Schefter also gave an update on Porter's contract talks with the Steelers on Monday.

Adam Schefter and Ian Rapoport of ESPN and NFL Network reported Sunday that a trade involving Porter "is very possible" as he and the Steelers continue to struggle to find common ground on a new contract.

Schefter and Rapoport noted that the two sides held negotiations until the day before the start of the season, but Pittsburgh does not want to continue contract talks during the campaign. According to the two insiders, Porter and the Steelers "remain far apart on a deal."

Porter previously requested a trade from Pittsburgh and is open to playing for another team, according to Schefter and Rapoport. The Steelers are asking for a premium draft pick, perhaps in the first round, but there has been no "notable interest" so far.

Porter is playing in the final year of his rookie deal and has a $3.9 million base salary for the 2026 season. He's coming off a solid season that saw him record 52 tackles, a sack and 14 passes defended, so he's bound to get a lucrative deal when the time comes.

Whether that deal comes from the Steelers or another team remains to be seen.

New England Patriots cornerback Christian Gonzalez and Seattle Seahawks corner Devon Witherspoon reset the market this offseason when they signed new deals that average more than $33 million annually.

As it stands now, Porter might not be worth that kind of money, but if he puts together a strong 2026 season, he could command that number or more when he reaches free agency.

Porter might hope to find another team to spend the 2026 campaign with, but right now, it seems Pittsburgh hasn't gained much traction in finding a trade for him.

Whether he'll be on the field for the Steelers in Week 2 against the New England Patriots remains to be seen.

articles.title: Michael Penix Jr., Tua Injury Updates in New Rumors on Falcons QBs for Week 2 vs. Panthers
articles.summary: The Atlanta Falcons are still facing plenty of quarterback uncertainty heading into their Week 2 game against the Carolina Panthers with Michael Penix Jr. and Tua Tagovailoa dealing with injuries.
articles.body:
The Atlanta Falcons are still facing plenty of quarterback uncertainty heading into their Week 2 game against the Carolina Panthers with Michael Penix Jr. and Tua Tagovailoa dealing with injuries.

"The Falcons would like Michael Penix to be their starting quarterback when he is healthy, when he is ready and when he can do it," NFL Network's Ian Rapoport reported Monday. "From what I understand, the original timeframe here was about Week 2 or 3, which makes sense. They did not put him on IR to begin the season, believing that he could be back in that window.

"It seems at this point, we'll see, that it might be a bit too early for Michael Penix. … He's got to work himself back and feel comfortable being out there."

As for Tagovailoa, Rapoport described him as "day-to-day" with an oblique injury but added, "generally, for a throwing position, it's not usually one week. So if he can't go, then you'll see Cooper Rush out there again."

With Penix still recovering from the torn ACL he suffered last season and Tagovailoa sidelined with his setback, Rush was thrown into a starting role during Week 1 against the Pittsburgh Steelers.

He didn't exactly thrive, going 12-of-22 for 143 yards, one touchdown and two interceptions, one of which was returned for a touchdown by T.J. Watt. While asking a third-string quarterback who just signed with the team in July to do too much isn't completely fair, the Falcons may have won if he just protected the ball.

He at least got the ball into the team's top playmaker's hands, as Bijan Robinson finished with 83 rushing yards, 90 receiving yards and a touchdown.

Maintaining that strategy against a Panthers defense that just gave up 59 points to the Chicago Bears could keep the Falcons in the game or perhaps even be enough to win and improve to 1-1 on the season.

But the NFC South team surely wants to see what it has in Penix for the long-term future after using the No. 8 overall pick of the 2024 NFL draft on him.

For now, though, it may still be Rush under center.

articles.title: Does the NFL's double digit ratings decline for opener show fan fatigue?
articles.summary: The New England Patriots-Seattle Seahawks opener drew 25.1 million viewers on NBC and Peacock, a 12% drop tied to the NFL's Wednesday gamble.
articles.body: The New England Patriots-Seattle Seahawks matchup last week was the NFL’s lowest-rated opening-night game since 2022, averaging 25.1 million viewers on NBC and Peacock. That figure represents a 12% decline from last season’s Dallas Cowboys-Philadelphia Eagles opener, which drew 28.3 million viewers on the same network. Considering recent changes to Nielsen’s measurement system, the broader multiyear decline and the double-digit year-over-year drop are notable. The NFL and NBC will likely attribute the decline, at least in part, to the opener airing on a Wednesday for the first time. Moving the game from Thursday, traditionally a stronger night for viewership, to Wednesday was likely a factor — perhaps a significant one. But that is more a consequence than an excuse. NFL’S GROSSLY EXPANDED NATIONAL SCHEDULE IS MAKING REDZONE AND SUNDAY TICKET LESS ESSENTIAL To understand why the NFL opened the season on a Wednesday, consider the league’s broader strategy. The NFL views streaming and international games as its two biggest avenues for growth. But the Sports Broadcasting Act of 1961 prohibits televised NFL games on most Friday nights during the high school and college football seasons. As a result, the league could not schedule the Los Angeles Rams-San Francisco 49ers game in Australia on Friday, as it had the previous two seasons. Instead, the game was played on Thursday, pushing the Patriots-Seahawks opener on NBC to Wednesday. The NFL will also play another Wednesday game on Netflix on the night before Thanksgiving. There will be four Friday games this season, including one on Black Friday and three on Christmas Day. Nine games will be played internationally. On one hand, the expanded schedule means more football on television. On the other, it could lead to lower-quality football. NFL SUNDAY TICKET IS NO LONGER WORTH THE PRICE | BOBBY BURACK Fans saw last season how the additional windows, unusual days of the week, extensive travel, and limited rest hindered the quality of play. Teams playing on short rest, sometimes overseas, frequently looked sloppy and unprepared. The changes also diminished the games’ sense of occasion. The Sunday slate, in particular, has become increasingly diluted by the addition of newly created national windows. It should come as no surprise that fewer people watched last Wednesday’s opener than in previous years. Patriots-Seahawks was a sluggish snoozefest through three quarters. Working Americans faced two additional days of early wake-up calls that week. Another primetime game (Rams-49ers) followed the next night. There is no reason to overstate the significance of the ratings decline. The game still averaged more than 25 million viewers. That is more than any NBA Finals game drew in June. The NFL is the most popular form of entertainment in the country. Still, signs of fan fatigue and frustration are growing. We have not even discussed how expensive it is to follow the NFL across its various television networks and streaming services this season. And it is expensive. There is a reason the television networks did not cave and negotiate new rights deals with the league early, as some media analysts predicted. Put plainly, there is more resistance to the NFL’s insatiable appetite for growth than the league may realize. The NFL appears to believe that standard does not apply to it. Based on recent viewership trends, the league is slightly overconfident.

articles.title: ESPN, NFL Network now simulcast the same Monday night pregame show
articles.summary: For years, NFL fans who wanted to watch a Monday Night Football pregame show had their pick of two different options.
articles.body:
For years, NFL fans who wanted to watch a Monday Night Football pregame show had their pick of two different options. Now? Not.

Monday Night Countdown, ESPN's longtime pregame show, is now shown on both ESPN and NFL Network, as a result of the deal that made ESPN the owner of NFL Media and the NFL a 10 percent owner of ESPN.

It's easy to see why ESPN and the NFL see this as a good thing, a cost-cutting move that means they're only producing one show instead of two.

For fans, however, fewer choices is a bad thing. Some fans preferred the NFL Network pregame show, which is now gone. And even for viewers who were watching Monday Night Countdown anyway, there are legitimate concerns that the stronger ties between ESPN and the NFL will mean even less independence in the coverage of the sport. More propaganda, less journalism.

Ultimately, the ESPN-NFL Media merger wasn't done for the fans. It was done for the bottom lines of ESPN and NFL Media, who can save money on production costs when putting one show on two channels.
